questions.explanation:
All network interfaces assigned to an Azure application security group must be in the same virtual network as the first interface assigned to that group. ASG1 is assigned to NIC1 in VNET1, so it can also be assigned to NIC2 and NIC3, which are in VNET1. NIC4 and NIC5 are in different virtual networks.

**Learn more:** [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to collaborate with a partner organization that has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
Fabrikam.com uses these identity providers:  
  
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP)  
- Microsoft accounts  
- Microsoft Entra ID  
  
You need to configure the Cross-tenant access settings for B2B collaboration.  
  
Which identity providers support cross-tenant access?

options.text: GCP and Microsoft Entra ID only
Microsoft accounts and Microsoft Entra ID only
GCP, Microsoft accounts, and Microsoft Entra ID

questions.explanation:
Cross-tenant access settings control B2B collaboration with external Microsoft Entra organizations. Google and Microsoft accounts are supported as external identity providers for guest sign-in, but cross-tenant access settings apply only to Microsoft Entra tenants.

**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/what-is-b2b)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],After creating a new Azure subscription, you are tasked with ensuring that custom alert rules can be created in Azure Security Center.  
  
You have created an Azure Storage account.  
  
Which action should you take?

options.text: You should make sure that Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection is removed.
You should create a DLP policy.
You should create an Azure Log Analytics workspace.
You should make sure that Security Center has the necessary tier configured.

questions.explanation:
Custom log-based alert rules require a Log Analytics workspace as the target data store for collected logs and queries. Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center) integrates with Log Analytics, and Azure Monitor creates custom log-search alert rules against that workspace.

**Learn more:** [View exported data in Azure Monitor - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/continuous-export-view-data) · [Log Analytics workspace overview - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-workspace-overview)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
Your company uses an Azure Container Registry.  
  
You must assign a user a role that permits uploading images to the Azure Container Registry. The assigned role must provide no more privileges than necessary.  
  
Which of the following roles should you assign?
questions.explanation:
The `AcrPush` role grants data-plane permission to push and pull container images and artifacts, without granting Azure resource-management permissions. `AcrPull` is limited to pulling images, while `Contributor` and `Owner` provide broader privileges than required.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Container Registry Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure environment.  
  
You need to identify Azure configurations and workloads that do not comply with ISO 27001:2013 standards.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud uses its Regulatory compliance dashboard to assess Azure resources against regulatory standards and controls, reporting resources that are compliant or non-compliant. ISO 27001:2013 is available as an Azure Policy regulatory-compliance initiative for assessing relevant Azure configurations and workloads.

**Learn more:** [Regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Details of the ISO 27001:2013 Regulatory Compliance built-in initiative](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/samples/iso-27001)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure web app named App1 and a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs Microsoft SQL Server and connects to a virtual network named VNet1. App1, VM1, and VNet1 are located in the US Central Azure region.  
  
You need to make sure that App1 can connect to VM1. The solution must minimize costs.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Regional virtual network integration lets an Azure App Service app make outbound connections to resources in a virtual network in the same region, including a VM running SQL Server. It avoids the virtual network gateway and associated cost required for gateway-required integration.

**Learn more:** [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration) · [Configure gateway-required virtual network integration for your app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-gateway-required-vnet-integration)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy a new Conditional Access policy named CAPolicy1.  
  
You need to use the What If tool to evaluate how CAPolicy1 will affect users. The solution must minimize CAPolicy1's impact on users.  
  
What should you set the **Enable policy** setting for CAPolicy1 to?
questions.explanation:
Report-only mode evaluates and reports the outcome of a Conditional Access policy without enforcing its controls during sign-ins. It is included in What If evaluations, whereas a policy set to Off is not, so it permits impact assessment while avoiding disruption to users.\
\
**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Conditional Access Policies with the What If Tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/what-if-tool) · [Analyze Conditional Access Policy Impact](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-report-only)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy a new Conditional Access policy named CAPolicy1.  
  
You need to use the What If tool to evaluate how CAPolicy1 will affect users. The solution must minimize CAPolicy1's impact on users.  
  
What should you set the **Enable policy** setting for CAPolicy1 to?

options.text: Turn on the system-assigned managed identity for Contoso1812.
Scale out the App Service plan of Contoso1812.
Add a deployment slot to Contoso1812.
Scale up the App Service plan of Contoso1812.
Upload a PFX file to Contoso1812.

questions.explanation:
An App Service custom domain must be added as a hostname on the web app after its DNS mapping is configured. HTTPS on that custom hostname also requires a TLS/SSL certificate bound to the hostname; a PFX file supplies a bring-your-own certificate. An S1 App Service plan supports the required SSL binding.

**Learn more:** [Overview of using custom domain names in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-custom-domains) · [Secure your domain with TLS/SSL in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-bindings)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 15 Azure virtual machines in a resource group called RG1.  
  
All of the virtual machines run the same applications.  
  
You need to stop unauthorized applications and malware from running on the virtual machines.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Apply an Azure policy to RG1.
From Azure Security Center, configure adaptive application controls.
Configure Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection.
Apply a resource lock to RG1.

questions.explanation:
Adaptive application controls use observed workloads to generate an allow list of known-safe applications for virtual machines and identify execution of applications outside that list. This application allow-listing capability is designed to protect machines from unauthorized software and malware.

**Learn more:** [Reference table for all compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute) · [Azure security baseline for Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/baselines/virtual-machines-windows-virtual-machines-security-baseline)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Container Registry named `Registry1`.  
  
From Azure Security Center, you enable Azure Container Registry vulnerability scanning for the images in `Registry1`.  
  
You perform the following actions:  
  
- Push a Windows image named `Image1` to `Registry1`.  
- Push a Linux image named `Image2` to `Registry1`.  
- Push a Windows image named `Image3` to `Registry1`.  
- Modify `Image1` and push the new image as `Image4` to `Registry1`.  
- Modify `Image2` and push the new image as `Image5` to `Registry1`.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953697497-1njlra9m.png)  
  
Which two images will be scanned for vulnerabilities? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Security Center vulnerability scanning for Azure Container Registry automatically scans supported Linux images when they are pushed to the registry. Therefore, the Linux images `Image2` and `Image5` are scanned; the Windows images are not.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for container registries - benefits and features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-container-registries-introduction) · [Security considerations for container instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-image-security)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must evaluate the underlined segment to determine whether it is correct.  
  
You have been assigned to create a separate subscription for every division in your company. However, all subscriptions will be associated with one Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that every subscription has the same role assignments.  
  
You use Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Select `No adjustment required` if the underlined segment is correct. If it is incorrect, select the correct option.
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Privileged Identity Management provides eligible and time-bound Azure RBAC role assignments, whereas Azure Blueprints supports role-assignment artifacts that can be applied to subscriptions to standardize access assignments.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Blueprints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/overview) · [Eligible and time-bound role assignments in Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/pim-integration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the Azure App Service web apps displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783965706894-kfa3zzc6.png)  
  
You upload a private-key certificate named Cert1.pfx to App1.  
  
Which apps can use Cert1?
questions.explanation:
Private certificates uploaded or imported to Azure App Service are shared only with app services in the same deployment unit (webspace), which is bound to the App Service plan's resource group, region, and operating-system combination. Only App1 matches RG1, East US, and Windows; App2 has Linux, App3 is in RG2, and App4 is in Central US.

**Learn more:** [Install a TLS/SSL certificate for your app - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate?tabs=apex%2Crbac)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure SQL database and implement Always Encrypted.  
  
You need to ensure that application developers can retrieve and decrypt data in the database.  
  
Which two pieces of information should you give the developers? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Always Encrypted encrypts data with a column encryption key, which is itself protected by a column master key held in an external key store. An Always Encrypted-enabled client driver must be able to access the column master key to decrypt the column encryption key and return plaintext data. Developers therefore require the column master key and credentials that authorize its use.

**Learn more:** [Always Encrypted – How queries against encrypted columns work](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/always-encrypted-how-queries-against-encrypted-columns-work?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Create and store column master keys for Always Encrypted](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/create-and-store-column-master-keys-always-encrypted?view=sql-server-ver17)

questions.question:
You are investigating a security issue with an Azure Storage account.  
  
You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account. What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics diagnostic logs are stored as blobs in the storage account's `$logs` container. AzCopy can download those log blobs for review and analysis.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
You are investigating a security issue with an Azure Storage account.  
  
You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account. What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
An Azure AD application registration must contain a reply URL (redirect URI), because the OAuth 2.0 implicit flow returns access tokens only to a registered endpoint. The identity platform rejects a return URI that does not match the app registration.

**Learn more:** [Redirect URI (reply URL) best practices and limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reply-url) · [Microsoft identity platform and OAuth 2.0 implicit grant flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-implicit-grant-flow)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953083046-ojndo3g2.png)  
  
Each virtual machine has one network interface.  
  
You add VM1's network interface to an application security group named ASG1.  
  
You need to identify the virtual machines whose network interfaces can be added to ASG1.  
  
What should you identify?
questions.explanation:
Network interfaces added to an Azure application security group must be in the same virtual network and Azure location as the interface already assigned to the group. Because VM1 is in West US 2 and VNET1, VM2 and VM3 qualify; being in a different subnet does not prevent membership.

**Learn more:** [Create, Change, or Delete Azure Network Interfaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-network-interface?tabs=network-interface-cli)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
In Azure Security Center, you create a custom alert rule.  
  
You need to configure the users who receive an email message when the alert is triggered.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Azure Monitor, create an action group.
From Security Center, modify the Security policy settings of the Azure subscription.
From Azure Active Directory (Azure AD), modify the members of the Security Reader role group.
From Security Center, modify the alert rule.

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor action groups define the notification recipients and actions for alerts, including email notifications. Associate the action group with the custom alert rule so its configured users receive the email when the alert fires.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and manage action groups in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/action-groups)

questions.question:
In Azure Security Center, you create a custom alert rule.  
  
You need to configure the users who receive an email message when the alert is triggered.  
  
What should you do?
questions.explanation:
A redirect URI identifies the approved destination to which Microsoft Entra ID sends security tokens after authentication. It must be configured for an application that obtains access tokens through a browser-based OAuth flow; public mobile clients do not use a client secret for this purpose.

**Learn more:** [Using redirect URIs with MSAL for iOS and macOS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/msal/objc/redirect-uris-ios)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to fulfill the technical requirements for VNetwork1. What should you do first?

options.text: Create a new subnet on VNetwork1.
Remove the NSGs from Subnet11 and Subnet13.

questions.explanation:
The scenario's technical requirements call for deploying Azure Firewall to VNetwork1. Azure Firewall must be placed in its own dedicated subnet that is named exactly 'AzureFirewallSubnet' (minimum size /26), separate from any other subnet used by workloads or NSG-protected resources. Since VNetwork1 does not yet have this subnet, it must be created first, before Azure Firewall can be deployed and before any dependent configuration (such as routing traffic through the firewall) can be completed. This makes creating a new subnet on VNetwork1 the necessary first step, ahead of any NSG adjustments on Subnet11, Subnet12, or Subnet13, or configuring DDoS protection.

**Learn more:** [Deploy & configure Azure Firewall using the Azure portal | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-deploy-portal) · [Azure Firewall FAQ | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/firewall-faq)

You have an Azure subscription containing virtual machines.  
  
You enable just-in-time (JIT) VM access on all the virtual machines.  
  
You need to connect to a virtual machine by using Remote Desktop.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Azure Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM), activate the Security administrator user role.
From Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM), activate the Owner role for the virtual machine.
From the Azure portal, select the virtual machine, select Connect, and then select Request access.
From the Azure portal, select the virtual machine and add the Network Watcher Agent virtual machine extension.

questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access requires a request that temporarily opens the configured inbound RDP port for the requesting source IP and approved time period. From the virtual machine's Azure portal Connect page, select **Request access** before connecting through RDP.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Connect using Remote Desktop to an Azure VM running Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/connect-rdp)

questions.question:
Your network has an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain that synchronizes with an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You plan to implement single sign-on (SSO) for Azure AD resources.  
  
You need to configure an Intranet Zone setting for every user by using a Group Policy Object (GPO).  
  
Which setting should you configure?

options.text: Allow updates to status bar via script

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra seamless SSO requires the Microsoft Entra autologon URL to be placed in users’ Local Intranet zone and requires the Intranet Zone Group Policy setting **Allow updates to status bar via script** to be enabled.\
\
**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Microsoft Entra seamless single sign-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sso-quick-start)

questions.question:
Your company’s Azure subscription contains 100 virtual machines with Azure Diagnostics enabled.  
  
You need to analyze the security events from a Windows Server 2016 virtual machine and have already opened Azure Monitor.  
  
Which of the following options should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor Logs is the query interface for collected Windows security-event records, such as those in the `SecurityEvent` table. Metrics are numerical measurements, while the Activity Log records Azure resource-management operations rather than guest operating system security events.\
\
**Learn more:** [SecurityEvent — Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables/securityevent) · [Activity log in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/platform/activity-log)

Your company’s Azure subscription contains 100 virtual machines with Azure Diagnostics enabled.  
  
You need to analyze the security events from a Windows Server 2016 virtual machine and have already opened Azure Monitor.  
  
Which of the following options should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Data Lake Storage directory operations require a private endpoint for the Data Lake Storage (`dfs`) subresource. A private endpoint for the Blob (`blob`) subresource is also required because requests targeting the Data Lake Storage endpoint can be redirected to the Blob endpoint. Therefore, two private endpoints ensure all listed operations can complete securely.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints)

questions.explanation: The built-in **Enable Monitoring in Azure Security Center** initiative groups the Azure Policy definitions used to enable and configure default security monitoring for resources in a subscription. Reviewing that initiative identifies the security settings assigned by default.

You plan to deploy an app that will modify Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) user properties by using Microsoft Graph.  
  
You need to ensure that the app can access Azure AD. What should you configure first?

options.text: a custom role-based access control (RBAC) role

questions.explanation:
A user-defined route can force traffic to a network virtual appliance by setting VM1 as the virtual-appliance next hop. A default route with the 0.0.0.0/0 address prefix directs all matching traffic through that appliance. Network security groups filter traffic rather than route it, and system routes are Azure-managed default routes.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster that must connect to an Azure Container Registry.  
  
You need to use the AKS cluster’s automatically generated service principal to authenticate to the Azure Container Registry.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: a secret in Azure Key Vault
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) user
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) group

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Registry access for a service principal is granted through Azure RBAC. Assigning the service principal an appropriate registry role—such as `AcrPull` for pull access on a non-ABAC-enabled registry—authorizes the AKS cluster to retrieve container images.

**Learn more:** [Service Principal Authentication for Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-auth-service-principal) · [Azure Container Registry Microsoft Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have been assigned to create an Azure key vault by using PowerShell. You have been told that objects deleted from the key vault must be retained for a defined period of 90 days.  
  
Which two of the following parameters must be used together to satisfy the requirement? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Soft delete retains deleted Key Vault objects for the retention period, while purge protection prevents permanent deletion during that retention period and requires soft delete. The deployment parameters do not provide deletion retention or purge protection.

**Learn more:** [New-AzKeyVault (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/new-azkeyvault?view=azps-15.3.0&viewFallbackFrom=azps-15.1.0) · [Update-AzKeyVault (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/update-azkeyvault?view=azps-12.5.0)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a storage account named `storage1` and a virtual machine named `VM1`.  
  
`VM1` is connected to a virtual network named `VNet1`, which contains one subnet and uses Azure DNS.  
  
You need to ensure that `VM1` connects to `storage1` by using a private IP address. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: For storage1, disable public network access.
On VNet1, create a new subnet.
For storage1, create a new private endpoint.
Create an Azure Private DNS zone.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Storage private endpoint creates a network interface with a private IP address in the virtual network and provides private connectivity to the storage service through Azure Private Link. With Azure-provided DNS, the required private DNS zone and records can be created automatically, allowing the normal storage endpoint name to resolve to the private IP address.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-private-endpoints)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a storage account named `storage1` and two web apps named `app1` and `app2`.  
  
Both apps will write data to `storage1`.  
  
You need to ensure that each app can read only the data it wrote.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Provide each app with a system-assigned identity and configure storage1 to use Azure AD User account authentication.
Provide each app with a separate Storage account key and configure the app to send the key with each request.
Provide each app with a user-managed identity and configure storage1 to use Azure AD User account authentication.
Provide each app with a unique Base64-encoded AES-256 encryption key and configure the app to send the key with each request.

questions.explanation:
A system-assigned managed identity gives each web app its own Microsoft Entra security principal. Azure Storage can use Microsoft Entra authentication and Azure RBAC to grant each identity access only to that app’s permitted data scope. Storage account keys provide account-level Shared Key access, so separate keys do not isolate the apps’ data.

**Learn more:** [Authorize access to blobs using Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/authorize-access-azure-active-directory) · [Access Azure Storage from a web app using managed identities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/multi-service-web-app-access-storage)

questions.question:
You have an Azure web app named **webapp1**.  
  
You need to configure continuous deployment for **webapp1** by using an Azure Repo.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Azure Repos is hosted within an Azure DevOps organization. Before an Azure Repo can be selected as the continuous-deployment source for an App Service web app, an Azure DevOps organization must exist to contain the project and repository.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure continuous deployment to Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/deploy-continuous-deployment)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must meet the identity and access requirements for Group1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a membership rule to Group1.
Delete Group1. Create a new group named Group1 that has a group type of Microsoft 365. Add users and devices to the group.
Modify the membership rule of Group1.
Change the membership type of Group1 to Assigned. Create two groups that have dynamic memberships. Add the new groups to Group1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra dynamic membership supports a user-based rule or a device-based rule, but not a single rule containing both users and devices. Use separate dynamic groups for the San Francisco users and their devices, and add those security groups to Group1 after changing it to assigned membership. Security groups support nested security groups, whereas Microsoft 365 groups allow only user members.

**Learn more:** [Manage rules for dynamic membership groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership) · [Learn about group types, membership types, and access management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/concept-learn-about-groups)

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is associated with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com.  
  
An administrator named Admin1 has access to the following identities:  
  
- An OpenID-enabled user account  
- A Hotmail account  
- An account in contoso.com  
- An account in an Azure AD tenant named fabrikam.com  
  
You plan to use Azure Account Center to transfer ownership of Sub1 to Admin1.  
  
To which accounts can ownership of Sub1 be transferred?

options.text: contoso.com, fabrikam.com, Hotmail, and OpenID-enabled user account

questions.explanation:
Subscription billing ownership can be transferred to an eligible Microsoft account or Azure AD organizational account. An organizational account in either contoso.com or fabrikam.com is eligible, and a Hotmail account is a Microsoft account; an OpenID-enabled user account is not an eligible account type for this transfer.

**Learn more:** [Transfer billing ownership of an MOSP Azure subscription to another account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/billing-subscription-transfer)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com that includes a user named User1.  
  
You are planning to publish several applications within this tenant.  
  
You need to make sure that User1 is able to grant admin consent for these published applications.  
  
Which two user roles could you assign to User1 to accomplish this? (Each correct answer presents a complete solution.)
questions.explanation:
Admin consent for published applications can be granted by users assigned certain built-in Azure AD roles that include the permission to manage app permission grants for the entire organization. Both the Cloud Application Administrator and Application Administrator roles include this capability, allowing an assigned user to grant tenant-wide admin consent to registered/published applications, whereas Security Administrator, User Administrator, and Application Developer roles do not include this permission.

**Learn more:** [Azure AD built-in roles - Application Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/roles/permissions-reference) · [Configure how end-users consent to applications - grant admin consent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/manage-apps/configure-user-consent)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953363409-rh1hljba.png)  
  
In Azure Security Center, you enable Auto Provisioning. You then deploy the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953366594-kxe5wbyj.png)  
  
On which virtual machines is the Microsoft Monitoring Agent installed?
questions.explanation:
Azure Security Center Auto Provisioning automatically deploys the Log Analytics agent, formerly called the Microsoft Monitoring Agent (MMA), to Azure virtual machines in the subscription. It covers both the existing virtual machines and virtual machines deployed after Auto Provisioning is enabled; therefore, VM1, VM2, VM3, and VM4 receive the agent.

**Learn more:** [Reference table for compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute) · [Set-AzSecurityAutoProvisioningSetting (Az.Security)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.security/set-azsecurityautoprovisioningsetting?view=azps-15.3.0)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Azure Resource Manager templates to deploy Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to automatically disable unused Windows features as virtual machine instances are provisioned.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: device configuration policies in Microsoft Intune
an Azure Desired State Configuration (DSC) virtual machine extension
security policies in Azure Security Center

questions.explanation:
The Azure Desired State Configuration (DSC) virtual machine extension applies a PowerShell DSC configuration to a Windows VM. A DSC configuration can manage Windows features, including ensuring that unused features are absent, and the extension can be included in an Azure Resource Manager template for deployment-time configuration.

**Learn more:** [Azure Desired State Configuration Extension Handler](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/dsc-windows) · [Desired State Configuration extension with Azure Resource Manager templates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/dsc-template)

questions.question:
You have been asked to delegate administrative access to your company’s Azure Key Vault.  
  
You must ensure that a specific user can add and delete certificates in the Key Vault, while assigning access according to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which of the following options should you use to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Key Vault access policy can grant a named user only the required certificate permissions, including `create` and `delete`, without granting unrelated permissions for keys, secrets, or broader vault administration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Certificate access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/certificates/certificate-access-control) · [Assign an Azure Key Vault access policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/assign-access-policy)

You intend to use Azure Resource Manager templates to carry out multiple deployments of identically configured Azure virtual machines. The administrator-account password for every deployment is stored as a secret in different Azure key vaults.  
  
You need to identify a way to dynamically construct a resource ID that designates the key vault containing the correct secret for each deployment.  
  
The key vault name and secret name will be supplied as inline parameters.  
  
What should you use to construct the resource ID?
questions.explanation:
A linked template supports dynamically generating the Key Vault resource ID from deployment parameters and passing that ID for the secret reference. ARM template expressions are not permitted in a parameters file, so it cannot construct the dynamic ID there.

**Learn more:** [Use Azure Key Vault to pass secure parameter value during deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/templates/key-vault-parameter)

You plan to deploy an Azure Private Link service named APL1.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have Azure Resource Manager templates that you use to deploy Azure virtual machines.  
  
You need to automatically disable unused Windows features as virtual-machine instances are provisioned.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: device configuration policies in Microsoft Intune
security policies in Azure Security Center
device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune

questions.explanation:
Azure Automation State Configuration applies PowerShell Desired State Configuration to Azure virtual machines and continually enforces their specified configuration. A DSC `WindowsFeature` resource can require a Windows feature to be absent, enabling unused features to be disabled automatically during VM deployment and configuration.

**Learn more:** [Azure Automation State Configuration overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-overview) · [Get started with Azure Automation State Configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-getting-started)

questions.question:
You are investigating a security issue involving an Azure Storage account.  
  
You enable diagnostic logging for the storage account. What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics logs are stored as blobs in the `$logs` container. AzCopy downloads this log data from the storage account for local review.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
You have been assigned to apply Conditional Access policies for your company’s current Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
The process includes evaluating risk events and risk levels. Which of the following risk levels should be configured for users whose credentials have leaked?
questions.explanation:
A leaked-credentials detection is always classified as high risk because Microsoft has confirmed that valid credential material was exposed, rather than merely observing a heuristic or probabilistic signal.\
\
**Learn more:** [Risk detection types and levels - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-risk-detection-types)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) role assignment.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Pulling images from Azure Container Registry requires an Azure RBAC role assignment that grants the AKS service principal registry pull permissions, such as the `AcrPull` role for a non-ABAC registry. An Azure AD directory-role assignment does not provide that registry access.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Container Registry service principal authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-auth-service-principal) · [Azure Container Registry Microsoft Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

questions.question:
You need to satisfy the technical requirements for the finance department users.  
  
Which settings in CAPolicy1 should you modify?
questions.explanation:
A Conditional Access sign-in-frequency requirement, including requiring reauthentication after a defined interval for SharePoint Online, is configured through the policy’s Session controls. Microsoft Entra identifies sign-in frequency as a Session control that changes the default sign-in frequency for modern authentication.\
\
**Learn more:** [Build a Conditional Access policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies) · [Require reauthentication and disable browser persistence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-persistent-browser)

questions.question:
An Azure subscription contains an Azure Blob storage account named `blob1`.  
  
You need to configure attribute-based access control (ABAC) for `blob1`.  
  
Which attributes can be used in access conditions?

options.text: blob index tags and container names only
file extensions and container names only
blob index tags, file extensions, and container names

Azure Blob Storage ABAC conditions support blob index tags and the container name as attributes. File extension is not a separate supported attribute; blob path is the supported path-related resource attribute.\

You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Container Registry named Registry1. Microsoft Defender for Cloud is enabled for the subscription.  
  
You upload several container images to Registry1 and find that vulnerability security scans were not performed.  
  
You need to ensure that container images are vulnerability-scanned when they are uploaded to Registry1. What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure portal, modify the Pricing tier settings.
From Azure CLI, lock the container images.
Upload the container images by using AzCopy.
Push the container images to Registry1 by using Docker.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud scans Azure Container Registry images when they are pushed to the registry (and also supports other qualifying registry operations). A Docker push creates the image-push event that triggers vulnerability scanning; registry locks, AzCopy uploads, and the Azure Container Registry pricing tier do not provide that trigger.

**Learn more:** [Scan registry images with Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/scan-images-defender) · [Vulnerability assessments for Defender for Cloud supported environments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/agentless-vulnerability-assessment-azure)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure a delegated permission without admin consent.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Delegated permissions authorize an application to act on behalf of a signed-in user, within that user’s own access rights. Azure Key Vault exposes the `https://vault.azure.net/user_impersonation` scope, and eligible delegated permissions can be consented to by the user without tenant-wide administrator consent.\
\
**Learn more:** [Scopes and permissions in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/scopes-oidc) · [Overview of permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You set up a delegated permission with administrator consent.  
  
Does this solution achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Delegated permissions authorize an application to act on behalf of a signed-in user. Administrator consent grants the configured delegated permission for users in the tenant, enabling the delegated access model required for access on users’ behalf.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a resource group named RG1 and a security group named ServerAdmins. RG1 includes 10 virtual machines, a virtual network named VNET1, and a network security group (NSG) named NSG1. ServerAdmins can access the virtual machines by using RDP.  
  
You need to ensure that NSG1 permits RDP connections to the virtual machines for no more than 60 minutes when a ServerAdmins member requests access.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: an Azure policy assigned to RG1
a just in time (JIT) VM access policy in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role assignment
an Azure Bastion host on VNET1

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud just-in-time VM access can protect RDP port 3389 and set a maximum request time. Upon an approved request, it temporarily configures the relevant NSG to permit inbound RDP access for the configured duration, then restores the NSG state after that time expires.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Just-in-time machine access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises network and an Azure subscription.  
  
You have the Microsoft SQL Server instances shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783955730967-u8g53xu8.png)  
  
You plan to deploy Microsoft Defender for SQL.  
  
Which SQL Server instances will Microsoft Defender for SQL protect?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for SQL protects Azure SQL Managed Instance and supported SQL Server instances on Windows machines, including SQL Server on Azure virtual machines and supported on-premises Windows servers when they are onboarded as required. SQL Server running on RHEL is not included in the applicable Windows Server support for Defender for SQL Servers on Machines.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Microsoft Defender for Azure SQL Databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-sql-introduction) · [Enable Defender for SQL Servers on Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-sql-usage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is associated with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com.  
  
The company develops an application named App1, which is registered in Azure AD.  
  
You need to ensure that App1 can access secrets in Azure Key Vault on behalf of the application users.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: an application permission without admin consent
a delegated permission without admin consent
a delegated permission that requires admin consent
an application permission that requires admin consent

questions.explanation:
Delegated permissions let an application access a resource on behalf of a signed-in user; application permissions are used when an app acts without a user. Azure Key Vault provides the delegated `user_impersonation` scope, and this scenario does not inherently require administrator consent.

**Learn more:** [Overview of permissions and consent in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/permissions-consent-overview) · [Scopes and permissions in the Microsoft identity platform](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/scopes-oidc)

You plan to deploy Azure container instances.  
  
You have a containerized application composed of two containers: an application container and a validation container. The application container is monitored by the validation container. After every transaction, the validation container performs security checks by sending requests to the application container and waiting for responses.  
  
You need to ensure that the application container and the validation container are scheduled for deployment together. The containers must communicate with one another only on ports that are not externally exposed.  
  
What should you include in the deployment?
questions.explanation: An Azure Container Instances container group deploys related containers together on the same host. The containers share a network namespace and can communicate through localhost, allowing the validation container to reach the application container without exposing those ports externally.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure WebApp1 to meet the data and application requirements.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Choose two. Each correct selection is worth one point.)

options.text: Turn on the HTTPS Only protocol setting.
Set the Minimum TLS Version protocol setting to 1.2.
Change the pricing tier of the App Service plan.
Turn on the Incoming client certificates protocol setting.

questions.explanation:
To ensure that all traffic to the web app is encrypted and that only a minimum acceptable TLS protocol version is used, you must turn on the 'HTTPS Only' setting so that all HTTP requests are automatically redirected to HTTPS, and set the 'Minimum TLS Version' setting to 1.2 so that only connections using TLS 1.2 or higher are permitted. These two settings together enforce encrypted, secure connections to the App Service, satisfying data-in-transit and application security requirements. Uploading a certificate is only necessary for custom domain TLS bindings, changing the pricing tier affects scale/features rather than encryption, and client certificates are used for mutual authentication scenarios, not general TLS enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Enforce HTTPS and TLS version in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-bindings#enforce-tls-versions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You need to set up diagnostic settings for contoso.com. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- Retain logs for two years.  
- Query logs by using the Kusto query language.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
Where should the logs be stored?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Log Analytics workspace is the native destination for Microsoft Entra ID diagnostic logs and supports querying those logs with Kusto Query Language (KQL). Its retention can be configured for 730 days, which satisfies a two-year retention requirement without building additional streaming or archival-query infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Configure a Log Analytics workspace and a custom workbook](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/monitoring-health/tutorial-configure-log-analytics-workspace) · [Manage data retention in a Log Analytics workspace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
Solution: Create a policy initiative and an assignment scoped to the **Tenant Root Group** management group.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Policy initiative combines multiple policy definitions into a single assignment. A policy assignment made at the root management group applies throughout the directory hierarchy, including all child management groups and subscriptions in the Microsoft Entra tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [Organize your resources with management groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview) · [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a policy initiative and assignments scoped to resource groups.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Policy initiative groups policy definitions, but each assignment applies only to its assigned scope and its child resources. Resource-group-scoped assignments therefore cannot deploy the initiative to all three Azure subscriptions; assignments must be scoped to each subscription or to a management group containing them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Understand scope in Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/scope)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a policy definition and assignments that are scoped to resource groups.  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
questions.explanation:
A resource-group policy assignment applies only to that resource group and its child resources, not to other resource groups or subscriptions. To deploy multiple policy definitions together across three subscriptions, use an initiative assignment at a shared management-group scope (or assign it separately at each subscription scope).\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand scope in Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/scope) · [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an initiative and an assignment scoped to a management group.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Policy initiative groups multiple policy definitions into one unit. Assigning that initiative at a management-group scope applies it to the management group’s child subscriptions, enabling centralized deployment across all three subscriptions.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definition structure basics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/definition-structure-basics) · [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a resource graph along with an assignment that is scoped to a management group.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Policy initiative, also called a policy set, is the object that groups multiple policy definitions for management through a single assignment. Azure Resource Graph is a resource-querying service and does not create such a policy grouping. A management-group assignment can apply policy to child subscriptions, but it must assign a policy definition or initiative.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Understand scope in Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/scope)

questions.question:
You are investigating a security issue involving an Azure Storage account.  
  
You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account.  
  
What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics diagnostic logs are stored in the `$logs` blob container of the storage account. Microsoft Azure Storage Explorer can access and view these stored log blobs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1.  
  
In Microsoft Defender for Cloud, you have a workflow automation named WF1. WF1 is configured to send an email message to a user named User1.  
  
You need to change WF1 so that it sends email messages to a distribution group named Alerts.  
  
What should you use to modify WF1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud workflow automation triggers a consumption Logic App, and the email action—including its recipient—is configured in that Logic App. Azure Logic Apps Designer is therefore used to change the recipient to the Alerts distribution group.\
\
**Learn more:** [Workflow automation - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/workflow-automations)

In Microsoft Defender for Cloud, you have a workflow automation named WF1. WF1 is configured to send an email message to a user named User1.

What should you use to modify WF1?

questions.question:
Your organization has an Azure subscription named Sub1.  
  
You plan to create multiple security alerts by using Azure Monitor.  
  
You need to prepare Sub1 for these alerts.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace is the Azure Monitor data store for collected log data. Log-based security alerts query that workspace, so it must exist before the alert rules can be created.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a Log Analytics workspace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/quick-create-workspace) · [Tutorial: Create a log search alert for an Azure resource](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/tutorial-log-alert)

options.text: In Microsoft Visual Studio, modify the .webtest file.
Upload the .webtest file to Application Insights.
Register the web test app in Azure AD.
Add a plug-in to the web test app.

questions.explanation:
OAuth 2.0 client-secret authentication for unattended execution requires a confidential client application with an application (client) ID and a client secret. Registering the web test application in Microsoft Entra ID creates that client identity; it can then obtain access tokens without interactive user authentication.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra Authentication - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/app-service/configure-authentication-provider-aad)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to map online infrastructure and carry out vulnerability scanning for the following:  
  
- ASNs  
- Hostnames  
- IP addresses  
- SSL certificates  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM)

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM) continuously discovers and maps internet-exposed infrastructure. It supports discovery of ASNs, hosts, IP addresses, and SSL certificates, and provides vulnerability and exposure insights for the external attack surface.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/azure/external-attack-surface-management/overview) · [What is discovery?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/external-attack-surface-management/what-is-discovery)

You must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Internet-facing virtual machines must be protected by using network security groups (NSGs).  
- Disk encryption must be enabled on all the virtual machines.  
  
What is the minimum number of security policies that you need to create in Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
questions.explanation:
A single security policy assigned at the Subscription1 scope can contain the required NSG and disk-encryption controls. Policy assignment at that scope covers both RG1 and RG2 and their virtual machines, so one policy can govern both requirements across all VMs.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes a group named Group1.  
  
You need to make sure that Group1 members sign in using passwordless authentication.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure the Microsoft Authenticator authentication method policy.

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Authenticator authentication method policy can enable passwordless phone sign-in and target the enabled method to a specific group, such as Group1. Its authentication mode can be set to passwordless-only (`deviceBasedPush`) when required. [Microsoft Learn: Passwordless sign-in with Authenticator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/authentication/howto-authentication-passwordless-phone)

**Learn more:** [Passwordless sign-in with Authenticator - Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/authentication/howto-authentication-passwordless-phone) · [Manage authentication methods for Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-authentication-methods-manage)

You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud. The subscription includes the Azure Policy definitions shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960426076-n5o0uhce.png)  
  
Which definitions can be assigned as a security policy in Defender for Cloud?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud security policies are based on Azure Policy initiative definitions, which bundle one or more policy definitions. Individual Azure Policy definitions cannot be assigned as Defender for Cloud security policies. Both initiatives qualify: a Regulatory Compliance initiative supports Defender for Cloud regulatory-compliance assessment, and a Security Center initiative supports security-policy assessment.

**Learn more:** [Regulatory Compliance in initiative definitions - Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/regulatory-compliance) · [Azure Policy built-in definitions for Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/policy-reference)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that includes an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com and a resource group named RG1.  
  
You create a custom role named Role1 for contoso.com.  
  
Where can you use Role1 to delegate permissions?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Entra ID custom role is a directory role and can be assigned only within the Microsoft Entra tenant where it is defined. Azure subscription and resource-group permissions are delegated through Azure RBAC role definitions and assignments, not through Microsoft Entra directory custom roles.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Microsoft Entra role-based access control (RBAC)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/custom-overview) · [Azure custom roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You need to stop nonprivileged Azure AD users from creating service principals in Azure AD.  
  
What should you do in the tenant's Azure Active Directory admin center?

options.text: From the User settings blade, set Users can register applications to No.
From the Properties blade, set Access management for Azure resources to No.
From the User settings blade, set Restrict access to Azure AD administration portal to Yes.
From the Properties blade, set Enable Security defaults to Yes.

questions.explanation:
An application registration automatically creates a service principal in the tenant. Setting **Users can register applications** to **No** in User settings prevents nonprivileged users from registering applications and therefore from creating service principals through application registration.

**Learn more:** [How and why apps are added to Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-applications-are-added) · [Register a Microsoft Entra app and create a service principal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-create-service-principal-portal)

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You configure the subscription to use another Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
What are two possible effects of this change? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Role assignments at the subscription level are lost.
Virtual machine managed identities are lost.
Virtual machine disk snapshots are lost.

questions.explanation:
Changing a subscription to a different Azure AD tenant permanently deletes Azure RBAC role assignments from the source tenant, so subscription-level role assignments must be recreated. Managed identities associated with resources such as virtual machines do not transfer as functional identities; system-assigned identities must be re-enabled and user-assigned identities must be recreated. Existing Azure resources and their disk snapshots are retained.

**Learn more:** [Transfer an Azure subscription to a different Microsoft Entra directory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/role-based-access-control/transfer-subscription) · [Associate or add an Azure subscription to your Microsoft Entra tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-subscriptions-associated-directory)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that users cannot create passwords that include a variation of the word `contoso`.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Password Protection provides a custom banned password list for organization-specific terms such as company names. Its password-evaluation algorithm normalizes common character substitutions and evaluates variations of a banned term, so adding `contoso` protects against passwords based on that word.

**Learn more:** [Eliminate bad passwords using Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-password-ban-bad) · [Configure custom banned passwords for Microsoft Entra password protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-configure-custom-password-protection)

questions.question:
Solution: You begin by creating a custom sensitive information type.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation: A custom sensitive information type is used to identify particular content patterns. It does not create a custom sensitivity label; sensitivity labels must be created separately in the relevant information-protection labeling service.

questions.question:
Solution: You begin by changing the Security Center pricing tier.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Custom sensitivity labels are created and configured in the Microsoft Purview portal. Changing the Azure Security Center pricing tier does not create or configure a sensitivity label.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and configure sensitivity labels and their policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-za/purview/create-sensitivity-labels)

questions.question:
Solution: Begin by integrating Security Center with Microsoft Cloud App Security.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Custom sensitivity labels are created and configured in the Microsoft Purview portal. Integration between Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps does not create a custom sensitivity label.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create and configure sensitivity labels and their policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-za/purview/create-sensitivity-labels) · [Automatically apply sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/use-case-information-protection)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
A user named User1 is eligible for the Billing administrator role.  
  
You need to ensure that the role can be used for no more than two hours.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Update the end date of the user assignment.

questions.explanation:
PIM role activation settings contain the Activation maximum duration setting, which controls the maximum number of hours an eligible user’s role activation remains active. Set that duration to two hours for the Billing administrator role.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Azure resource role settings in PIM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-resource-roles-configure-role-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to evaluate the underlined segment to determine whether it is correct.  
  
You have configured an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster in your testing environment. You are now preparing to deploy the cluster to the production environment.  
  
After disabling HTTP application routing, you want to replace it with an application-routing solution that provides reverse proxy and TLS termination for AKS services through a single IP address. You must create an AKS Ingress controller.  
  
Select `No adjustment required` if the underlined segment is accurate. If it is inaccurate, select the correct option.
questions.explanation:
An AKS Ingress controller provides Layer 7 reverse-proxy routing and TLS termination, and it can expose multiple AKS services through one IP address. Network security groups and application security groups provide traffic filtering, while an Azure Basic Load Balancer provides Layer 4 load balancing rather than application-layer ingress capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Plan application networking for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) workloads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/plan-application-networking) · [Azure Kubernetes Service managed NGINX ingress with the application routing add-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/app-routing)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing two virtual machines, named VM1 and VM2, that run Windows Server 2019.  
  
You are implementing Update Management in Azure Automation and plan to create a new update deployment named Update1.  
  
You must ensure that Update1 meets these requirements:  
  
- Automatically apply updates to VM1 and VM2.  
- Automatically add any new Windows Server 2019 virtual machines to Update1.  
  
What should you include in Update1?

options.text: a security group that has a Membership type of Assigned
a security group that has a Membership type of Dynamic Device

questions.explanation:
An Update Management dynamic group query dynamically resolves the virtual machines targeted by an update deployment. It can match VM1 and VM2 and automatically include newly discovered Windows Server 2019 virtual machines that meet the query criteria at deployment time.

**Learn more:** [New-AzAutomationUpdateManagementAzureQuery](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.automation/new-azautomationupdatemanagementazurequery?view=azps-15.3.0)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure key vault named Vault1 and a virtual machine named VM1.  
  
VM1 is connected to a virtual network named VNet1.  
  
You need to permit access to Vault1 only from VM1.  
  
What should you do in Vault1's Networking settings?

options.text: From the Firewalls and virtual networks tab, add the IP address of VM1.
From the Private endpoint connections tab, create a private endpoint for VM1.
From the Firewalls and virtual networks tab, add VNet1.
From the Firewalls and virtual networks tab, set Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass this firewall to Yes for Vault1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault firewall rules can allow access from selected virtual networks and subnets. Adding VNet1 to the vault's firewall and virtual-network rules allows the VM's virtual network traffic while denying traffic from networks that are not allowed. Key Vault IP network rules do not accept private IP address ranges, so a VM's private address is not an appropriate rule.

**Learn more:** [Configure network security for Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/how-to-azure-key-vault-network-security) · [Add-AzKeyVaultNetworkRule (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/az.keyvault/add-azkeyvaultnetworkrule)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure SQL database named SQL1 and an Azure key vault named KeyVault1. KeyVault1 stores the keys shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783954842474-nct697fa.png)  
  
You need to configure Transparent Data Encryption (TDE). TDE will use a customer-managed key for SQL1.  
  
Which keys can you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Database Transparent Data Encryption with a customer-managed key supports asymmetric RSA or RSA-HSM TDE protector keys sized 2048 or 3072 bits. Therefore, the eligible keys are the 2048-bit RSA key and the 3072-bit RSA key; a 4096-bit RSA key and an elliptic-curve key are not supported.

**Learn more:** [Azure SQL transparent data encryption with customer-managed key](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-byok-overview?view=azuresql)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You have the management group hierarchy shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960426168-nwq76duh.png)  
  
You create the definitions shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960429014-taba3qha.png)  
  
You need to use Defender for Cloud to add a security policy.  
  
Which definitions can be used as a security policy?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud security policies use Azure Policy initiative definitions. Initiative1 is defined at the Tenant Root Group, so it is available for assignment to descendant subscription Sub1. Initiative2 is defined directly in Sub1 and is also available there. Policy1 is an individual policy definition rather than an initiative, and Initiative3 is defined in MG1, which is not an ancestor of Sub1. Azure Policy definitions can be assigned only at or below their definition location in the resource hierarchy.

**Learn more:** [Understand scope in Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/scope) · [Azure Policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783965522635-5ds2m1jq.png)  
  
You create an Azure DDoS Protection plan named DDoS1 in the West US Azure region.  
  
Which resources can be added to DDoS1?
questions.explanation:
An Azure DDoS Network Protection plan protects virtual networks and can be associated with virtual networks in different Azure regions. It cannot have an App Service web app added as a protected resource. Consequently, VNet1 and VNet2 can be associated with the plan.\
\
**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Create and configure Azure DDoS Network Protection using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ddos-protection/manage-ddos-protection)
