questions.question:
You have an on-premises network and an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966700379-dhsvhh0d.png)  
  
You plan to deploy a Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN between the on-premises network and VNet1.  
  
You need to recommend an Azure VPN Gateway SKU that meets these requirements:  
  
- Supports 1-Gbps throughput  
- Minimizes costs  
  
What should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
VpnGw2 supports an aggregate throughput benchmark of 1 Gbps. VpnGw1 supports only 650 Mbps, while VpnGw2AZ also supports 1 Gbps but includes zone redundancy, which is unnecessary for the stated requirements and does not minimize cost.\
\
**Learn more:** [About Azure VPN Gateway](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/vpn-gateway/vpn-gateway-about-vpngateways)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to create a workflow automation in Azure Security Center that automatically remediates a security vulnerability.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud workflow automation runs a Consumption Logic App when its trigger conditions are met. The Logic App defines the automated remediation actions, so it must be created before it can be associated with the workflow automation. [Workflow automation — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/workflow-automations)\
\
**Learn more:** [Workflow automation — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/workflow-automations)

questions.question:
You have an Azure virtual machine running Ubuntu 16.04-DAILY-LTS.  
  
You plan to deploy and configure an Azure Key Vault and enable Azure Disk Encryption for the virtual machine.  
  
Which of the following is **TRUE** regarding Azure Disk Encryption for a Linux VM?

options.text: It is NOT supported for basic tier VMs.
It is NOT supported for standard tier VMs.
OS drive encryption for Linux virtual machine scale sets is supported.

questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption is not available for Basic-tier Linux virtual machines. It supports eligible Standard-tier VMs, but does not support OS-drive encryption for Linux virtual machine scale sets or encryption of custom images on Linux VMs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Disk Encryption scenarios on Linux VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disk-encryption-linux)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1 and an Azure Container Registry named ContReg1.  
  
You enable content trust for ContReg1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create trusted images in ContReg1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two roles should you assign to User1? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
AcrPush grants the data-plane permission to push container images to the registry. AcrImageSigner grants the Docker Content Trust permissions needed to sign images and create trusted image metadata. Together, these roles allow creation of trusted images without the broader management permissions granted by Contributor.

**Learn more:** [Manage signed images by using Docker Content Trust in Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-content-trust) · [Azure Container Registry Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are testing an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster. The cluster configuration is shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966702319-vga1h7yy.png)  
  
You plan to deploy the cluster to production and disable HTTP application routing.  
  
You need to implement application routing that provides reverse proxying and TLS termination for AKS services by using a single IP address.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Azure Standard Load Balancer.
Install the container network interface (CNI) plug-in.
Create an Azure Basic Load Balancer.

questions.explanation:
An AKS ingress controller provides Layer 7 reverse-proxy routing and TLS termination for Kubernetes services. Ingress rules allow multiple services to be exposed through a single IP address. Azure Load Balancer is a Layer 4 service and does not provide those HTTP/S routing or TLS-termination capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for network resources in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/operator-best-practices-network) · [Create an unmanaged ingress controller in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/azure/azure-kubernetes/load-bal-ingress-c/create-unmanaged-ingress-controller)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953084084-pis1p5wd.png)  
  
Which user can enable Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM)?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Privileged Identity Management can be enabled by a Global Administrator, and the enabling administrator must use multifactor authentication. A subscription Owner role and the Authentication Administrator role do not grant this directory-level capability; a Global Administrator without MFA enabled does not meet the MFA requirement.

**Learn more:** [Start using Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started) · [Microsoft cloud security benchmark – Privileged Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/mcsb-privileged-access)

options.text: Create a custom sensitive information type.
Elevate access for global administrators in Azure AD.
Upgrade the pricing tier of the Security Center to Standard.
Enable integration with Microsoft Cloud App Security.

questions.explanation:
A custom sensitive information type provides the organization-specific classification rule used with sensitivity labels. Built-in sensitive information types cannot be edited; custom types can be created or copied from built-in types and tailored to the required detection criteria. Azure RBAC elevation, Defender for Cloud pricing, and Cloud App Security integration are not prerequisites for defining that classification rule.

**Learn more:** [Learn about sensitive information types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about) · [Customize a built-in sensitive information type](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sit-customize-a-built-in-sensitive-information-type)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question: You need to make sure that the security operations requirements can be met. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn on Auto Provisioning in Security Center.
Integrate Security Center and Microsoft Cloud App Security.
Upgrade the pricing tier of Security Center to Standard.
Modify the Security Center workspace configuration.

questions.explanation:
The Standard tier of Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center) provides advanced security capabilities, whereas the free tier provides only basic security features. Enabling the Standard tier is therefore the prerequisite before configuring advanced operational integrations, data collection, or automatic agent provisioning.\
\
**Learn more:** [Pricings - Get - REST API (Azure Defender for Cloud)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/defenderforcloud/pricings/get?view=rest-defenderforcloud-2024-01-01)

questions.question: You need to make sure that the security operations requirements can be met. What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the API permissions of App1.
Add App1 as an enterprise application.
Assign Admin1 the Cloud application administrator role.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID encrypts tokens by using the public key from a certificate registered with the application. Uploading an App1 certificate makes the encryption key available so token encryption can be enabled.

**Learn more:** [Configure token decryption in Microsoft.Identity.Web](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/msidweb/authentication/token-decryption) · [Microsoft identity platform certificate credentials](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/certificate-credentials)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure key vault and an Azure Storage account. The key vault contains customer-managed keys, and the storage account is configured to use the customer-managed keys stored in the key vault.  
  
You plan to store data in Azure by using the following services:  
  
- Azure Files  
- Azure Blob storage  
- Azure Table storage  
- Azure Queue storage  
  
Which two services support data encryption by using the keys stored in the key vault? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
When customer-managed keys are configured for an Azure Storage account, Blob storage and Azure Files data are automatically encrypted with those keys. Table and Queue storage are not automatically covered unless the storage account was created with account-scoped encryption-key support for those services.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for account encryption - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview) · [Create an account that supports customer-managed keys for tables and queues - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/account-encryption-key-create)

You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named Admin1 and a virtual machine named VM1. VM1 runs Windows Server 2019 and was deployed using an Azure Resource Manager template. VM1 is a member of the backend pool of a public Azure Basic Load Balancer.  
  
Admin1 reports that VM1 appears as **Unsupported** on the Just in time VM access blade of Azure Security Center.  
  
You need to ensure that Admin1 can enable just in time (JIT) VM access for VM1.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create and configure a network security group (NSG).
Create and configure an additional public IP address for VM1.
Replace the Basic Load Balancer with an Azure Standard Load Balancer.
Assign an Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 1 license to Admin1.

questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Azure Security Center) works by dynamically creating NSG allow rules that open management ports for a limited time. A VM shows as Unsupported in the JIT blade when it lacks an associated network security group on its NIC or subnet, since there is nothing for JIT to modify. Creating and configuring an NSG for VM1 makes it eligible for JIT VM access. The Load Balancer SKU, additional public IP addresses, and Azure AD Premium licensing do not affect JIT eligibility for a VM.

**Learn more:** [Secure your management ports with just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-usage)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have three on-premises servers—Server1, Server2, and Server3—running Windows Server 2019. Server1 and Server2 are on the internal network, while Server3 is on the perimeter network. All of the servers can access Azure.  
  
From Azure Sentinel, you install a Windows firewall data connector.  
  
You need to collect Microsoft Defender Firewall data from the servers for Azure Sentinel.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an event subscription from Server1, Server2, and Server3.
Install the On-premises data gateway on each server.
Install the Microsoft Monitoring Agent on each server.
Install the Microsoft Monitoring Agent on Server1 and Server2. Install the On-premises data gateway on Server3.

questions.explanation: The legacy Windows Firewall data connector collects each server’s local Microsoft Defender Firewall data through the Microsoft Monitoring Agent. Because every server has Azure connectivity, the agent must be installed on Server1, Server2, and Server3; an on-premises data gateway and Windows event subscriptions are not required.

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to add a custom security recommendation to Defender for Cloud. The recommendation must receive the subscription’s custom severity rating.  
  
What should you create?
questions.explanation:
A custom Azure Policy definition creates the recommendation logic and holds the Defender for Cloud `metadata.securityCenter` properties, including the custom `Severity` value. An initiative can group that policy definition into a custom standard, but the severity belongs on the policy definition.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create custom standards and recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure resource group that includes 100 virtual machines.  
  
You have an initiative named Initiative1 that contains multiple policy definitions. Initiative1 is assigned to the resource group.  
  
You need to determine which resources do **not** comply with the policy definitions.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Azure Security Center, view the Regulatory compliance assessment.
From the Policy blade of the Azure Active Directory admin center, select Compliance.
From Azure Security Center, view the Secure Score.
From the Policy blade of the Azure Active Directory admin center, select Assignments.

questions.explanation:
Azure Policy’s Compliance view displays compliance results for policy and initiative assignments, including the non-compliant resources evaluated under the assigned initiative. The Assignments view manages assignments rather than reporting per-resource compliance.

**Learn more:** [Get compliance data of Azure resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/how-to/get-compliance-data) · [Create a policy assignment to identify non-compliant resources using Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/assign-policy-portal)

You create an Azure Firewall policy with the rules shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783964135786-u21bvey7.png)  
  
In what order should the rules be processed?

  explanation={"Azure Firewall Policy evaluates rule collection types in this fixed order: DNAT (NAT), network, then application. Which resources can be assigned the Contributor role for VM1?

options.text: Group1, Managed1, VM1, and App1 only

questions.explanation:

Group1, Managed1, VM1, and App1 are valid principals; VM2 has no managed identity specified and is only a virtual machine resource.

You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure key vault.  
  
You create a storage account named storage1.  
  
You plan to store data in the following storage1 services:  
  
- Azure Files  
- Azure Blob storage  
- Azure Table storage  
- Azure Queue storage  
  
For which two services can you configure data encryption by using keys stored in the key vault? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault protect Blob storage and Azure Files when configured for the storage account. Table and Queue storage require the storage account to have been created with an account-scoped encryption key before they can use customer-managed keys.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview) · [Create an account that supports customer-managed keys for tables and queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/account-encryption-key-create)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960410820-jcjqts0t.png)  
  
Which computers support file integrity monitoring?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud file integrity monitoring supports Windows Server workloads and supported Linux server distributions, including Windows Server 2022 and SUSE Linux Enterprise Server. Windows 10 is not included as a supported server workload for this scenario.

**Learn more:** [Support for the Defender for Servers plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/support-matrix-defender-for-servers) · [Enable File Integrity Monitoring](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/file-integrity-monitoring-enable-defender-endpoint)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You collect events from Azure virtual machines in an Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You plan to create alerts based on those collected events. You need to determine which Azure services can be used to create the alerts.  
  
Which two services should you identify? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor creates log alert rules from Log Analytics queries and fires alerts when query results meet the configured condition. Azure Sentinel, now called Microsoft Sentinel, uses analytics rules to monitor log data and generate alerts for detected security events.

**Learn more:** [Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-platform-logs) · [Create and publish analytics rules for Microsoft Sentinel solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/isv/sentinel-analytic-rules-creation)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription linked to an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
From the Azure portal, you register an enterprise application. Which additional resource is created in Azure AD?
questions.explanation:
An enterprise application is the tenant-local representation of an application and is implemented as a service principal. The service principal provides the application's identity and defines its access within the Azure AD tenant.\
\
**Learn more:** [Application and service principal objects in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/app-objects-and-service-principals)

questions.question:
You intend to configure Azure Disk Encryption for VM4.  
  
Which key vault can store the encryption key?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption requires the key vault that manages its encryption keys and secrets to be in the same Azure region and subscription as the virtual machine. KeyVault1 is the eligible vault for VM4. [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disk-encryption-overview)\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable Azure Disk Encryption for Linux VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/linux/disk-encryption-overview)

questions.question:
You intend to configure Azure Disk Encryption for VM4.  
  
Which key vault can store the encryption key?

options.text: the Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) ID
the Key Vault managed storage account key

questions.explanation:
The integrated Qualys vulnerability scanner extension uses the Log Analytics workspace ID to identify its workspace and the workspace primary shared key as the protected authentication setting. These values allow the extension to register and operate for the virtual machines.

**Learn more:** [Enable vulnerability scanning with the integrated Qualys scanner (deprecated)](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/azure/defender-for-cloud/deploy-vulnerability-assessment-vm?view=aspnetcore-2.0)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to create a custom role-based access control (RBAC) role that grants permission to read the Azure Storage account.  
  
Which RBAC role-definition property should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage account read access is a control-plane permission, which belongs in the `Actions` array of a custom Azure RBAC role definition. `DataActions` is for data-plane operations on data within a resource, and `AssignableScopes` only determines where the role can be assigned.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure custom roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles)

questions.question:
You have 10 virtual machines on one subnet that uses a single network security group (NSG).  
  
You need to log network traffic to an Azure Storage account.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the Network Performance Monitor solution.
Create an Azure Log Analytics workspace.
Enable diagnostic logging for the NSG.

questions.explanation:
NSG flow logs capture information about IP traffic flowing through a network security group, including inbound and outbound flows and the applied rule decision, and send the flow data to an Azure Storage account.\
\
**Learn more:** [NSG Flow Logs Overview - Azure Network Watcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-overview) · [Create, change, enable, disable, or delete NSG flow logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/network-watcher/nsg-flow-logs-manage)

options.text: From AKS1, upgrade the version of Kubernetes.
From Azure AD, implement Azure AD Premium P2
From Azure AD, configure the User settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID User settings control whether users can register applications. Enabling or configuring that tenant-level capability allows the application registrations needed for Azure AD-integrated AKS access, without requiring a Kubernetes upgrade, cluster recreation, or a Premium P2 license.

**Learn more:** [Manage user profile information in the Microsoft Entra admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-to-manage-user-profile-info) · [Delegate app registration permissions in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

VM1 and VM2 both connect to VNET1 and are configured to use NSG1.  
  
You need to ensure that DB1 can be accessed only by VM1 and VM2.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: For NSG1, configure a rule that has a service tag.
Add the IP address range of VNET1 to the Firewall settings of DB1.
Configure DB1 to allow access from only VNET1.

questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB supports virtual-network access rules that restrict account access to selected virtual network subnets using the Azure Cosmos DB service endpoint. Configuring DB1 to allow access only from VNET1 restricts permitted network sources to that virtual network, whereas NSG and application security group settings do not control access to the Cosmos DB account itself. Cosmos DB IP firewall rules must not contain private IP addresses from a virtual network address range.

**Learn more:** [Configure IP firewall for Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-firewall) · [Virtual network access for Azure Cosmos DB account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-vnet-service-endpoint)

questions.question:
You need to make sure that User2 can implement PIM.  
  
What should you do first?

You have an Azure subscription that uses Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
A PIM user assigned the User Access Administrator role reports an authorization error when performing a role assignment or viewing the assignment list.  
  
You need to resolve the issue by ensuring that the PIM service principal has the appropriate permissions for the subscription. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the PIM service principal?
questions.explanation:
The PIM service principal (MS-PIM) must be assigned the User Access Administrator role at the subscription scope to access Azure role assignments for PIM operations. This role supplies the necessary access-management permissions without granting broad resource-management permissions.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot access to Azure resources denied in Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-troubleshoot)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Firewall Standard instance named AzFW1.  
  
You need to determine whether AzFW1 can use these features:  
  
- TLS inspection  
- Threat intelligence  
- The network intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDPS)  
  
What can you use?

options.text: TLS inspection and the IDPS only
threat intelligence and the IDPS only
TLS inspection, threat intelligence, and the IDPS

questions.explanation:
Azure Firewall Standard supports threat-intelligence filtering, including alert and deny modes. TLS inspection and network IDPS are available only with the Premium SKU.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall and traffic inspection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/azure-firewall) · [Azure Firewall Manager policy overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/policy-overview)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Firewall Standard instance named AzFW1.  
  
You need to determine whether AzFW1 can use these features:  
  
- TLS inspection  
- Threat intelligence  
- The network intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDPS)  
  
What can you use?
questions.explanation:
An Azure Synapse workspace using a managed virtual network accesses an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account privately by using a managed private endpoint. The endpoint connection must be approved on the storage account to establish the private link.

**Learn more:** [Create a Managed private endpoint to connect to your data source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/synapse-analytics/security/how-to-create-managed-private-endpoints) · [Azure Synapse Analytics security white paper: Network security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/synapse-analytics/guidance/security-white-paper-network-security)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure AD tenant containing the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783964525299-qhv4dja6.png)  
  
You must ensure that the users are unable to create app passwords. The solution must allow User1 to continue using the Mail and Calendar app.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign User1 the Authentication Policy Administrator role.
Configure a multi-factor authentication (MFA) registration policy.
From multi-factor authentication, configure the service settings.

questions.explanation:
The MFA service settings include the tenant-wide option that allows users to create app passwords for non-browser apps. Disabling that option prevents new app-password creation while existing app passwords continue to work, allowing continued access for an application already configured with one.

**Learn more:** [Configure app passwords for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-mfa-app-passwords)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant that includes a user named User1.  
  
You plan to enable passwordless authentication for the tenant.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can enable the combined registration experience. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?
questions.explanation:
Enabling combined registration is a tenant-wide user-feature configuration, not merely an operation to manage a user’s authentication methods. Authentication Administrator can view, set, and reset authentication methods for non-administrative users, while Privileged Role Administrator manages role assignments. Among the available roles, Global Administrator has the required tenant-wide administrative permissions. Microsoft Entra’s current role reference also distinguishes Authentication Administrator’s limited authentication-method scope from Global Administrator’s authority to manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra ID.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
Solution: Create an AKS Ingress controller.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An AKS Ingress controller routes inbound web traffic to services in an AKS cluster; it does not attach standalone Docker containers on a virtual machine to the virtual network. The Azure CNI plug-in is used to provide virtual-network networking to containers on a standalone Linux Docker host, allowing their traffic to originate through the subnet where the Azure Storage and Azure SQL service endpoints are configured.\
\
**Learn more:** [Deploy container networking for a stand-alone Linux Docker host](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/deploy-container-networking-docker-linux) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: Install the container network interface (CNI) plug-in.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Virtual Network CNI plug-in provides Docker containers with direct virtual-network attachment and virtual-network IP connectivity. Containers can therefore access Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database that are protected by service endpoints configured on the subnet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable containers to use Azure Virtual Network capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/container-networking-overview) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an application security group.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
An application security group only provides a logical grouping of network interfaces that can be referenced by network security group rules. It does not configure Docker container networking or enable container access to Azure Storage and Azure SQL through a virtual network service endpoint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

questions.question:
You have been assigned to ensure that you can modify operating system security configurations through Azure Security Center.  
  
To accomplish this goal, you must have the appropriate Azure Security Center pricing tier in place. Which of the following pricing tiers is required?
questions.explanation:
Azure Security Center’s Standard tier provides advanced security capabilities, whereas the Free tier provides basic security features only. Therefore, modifying operating system security configurations requires the Standard tier.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Cloud pricing tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/defenderforcloud/pricings/get?view=rest-defenderforcloud-2024-01-01)

questions.question:
You are investigating a security issue involving an Azure Storage account.  
  
You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account.  
  
What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics diagnostic logs are saved as blobs in the `$logs` container of the storage account. Azure Storage Explorer can browse the storage account and retrieve or view those log blobs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant containing the identities shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957442710-mvlgfxlv.png)  
  
You plan to deploy Azure AD Identity Protection.  
  
What is the maximum number of user risk policies that you can configure?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Identity Protection supports one tenant-wide legacy user risk policy. It can target users and groups, but the tenant’s identity counts do not change that policy limit. Microsoft’s current guidance identifies the legacy User risk policy as a single policy type and recommends migrating it to Conditional Access before its retirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Risk policies - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure SQL Database server called SQL1.  
  
For SQL1, you enable Azure Defender for SQL to detect every threat-detection type.  
  
Which action will Azure Defender for SQL identify as a threat?

options.text: A user updates more than 50 percent of the records in a table.
A user attempts to sign in as SELECT * FROM table1.
A user is added to the db_owner database role.
A user deletes more than 100 records from the same table.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Azure SQL Databases detects potential SQL injection attacks, including malformed or malicious SQL statements generated through application input. Using `SELECT * FROM table1` as a sign-in attempt is indicative of a SQL injection payload.

**Learn more:** [Benefits and Features of Defender for Azure SQL Databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-sql-introduction) · [Alerts for SQL Database and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-sql-database-and-azure-synapse-analytics)

You have an Azure subscription that includes several Azure SQL databases and an Azure Sentinel workspace.  
  
You need to create a saved query in the workspace to identify events reported by Azure Defender for SQL.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From Azure CLI, run the Get-AzOperationalInsightsWorkspace cmdlet.
From the Azure SQL Database query editor, create a Transact-SQL query.
From the Azure Sentinel workspace, create a Kusto query language query.
From Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), create a Transact-SQL query.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel uses Kusto Query Language (KQL) to query and analyze data in its Log Analytics workspace. Events reported by Azure Defender for SQL are queried from that workspace with a saved KQL query.

**Learn more:** [Common tasks with KQL for Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/tutorials/common-tasks-microsoft-sentinel?view=microsoft-sentinel) · [Kusto Query Language overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/kusto/query/?view=microsoft-fabric)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription called Sub1. Sub1 includes a virtual network named VNet1, which has one subnet called Subnet1.  
  
Subnet1 hosts an Azure virtual machine named VM1 that runs Ubuntu Server 18.04.  
  
You create a Microsoft.Storage service endpoint in Subnet1.  
  
You need to ensure that, when Docker containers are deployed to VM1, the containers can access Azure Storage resources through the service endpoint.  
  
What should you do on VM1 before deploying the container?

options.text: Create an application security group and a network security group (NSG).
Install the container network interface (CNI) plug-in.

questions.explanation:
The Azure CNI plug-in attaches Docker containers to the Azure virtual network and assigns them virtual-network IP addresses. This lets container traffic use the network capabilities available to the subnet, including its Microsoft.Storage service endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Deploy container networking for a stand-alone Linux Docker host](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/deploy-container-networking-docker-linux) · [Deploy the Azure Virtual Network container network interface plug-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/deploy-container-networking)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You create a new Azure subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that you can create custom alert rules in Azure Security Center.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: Onboard Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection.
Create an Azure Log Analytics workspace.
Upgrade the pricing tier of Security Center to Standard.

questions.explanation:
Security Center custom alert rules use queries over data in an Azure Log Analytics workspace, so a workspace is required. The feature required the paid Security Center Standard tier; the Free tier did not provide the necessary capability.

**Learn more:** [Detecting in-memory attacks with Sysmon and Azure Security Center](https://azure.microsoft.com/de-de/blog/detecting-in-memory-attacks-with-sysmon-and-azure-security-center/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have 10 on-premises servers running Windows Server 2019.  
  
You plan to implement Azure Security Center vulnerability scanning for these servers.  
  
What should you install on the servers first?

options.text: the Azure Arc enabled servers Connected Machine agent
the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint agent
the Security Events data connector in Azure Sentinel
the Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager client

questions.explanation:
For on-premises servers, Azure Security Center vulnerability scanning requires the machines to first be onboarded to Azure Arc. Installing the Azure Arc-enabled servers Connected Machine agent registers each server as an Azure Arc-enabled machine, allowing the vulnerability-assessment extension to be deployed and managed from Azure.

**Learn more:** [Enable vulnerability scanning with the integrated Qualys scanner (deprecated)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/deploy-vulnerability-assessment-vm) · [Connect on-premises machines to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-machines)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to create an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster in an Azure subscription.  
  
The manifest for the registered server application is displayed in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953190867-4q2y31k4.png)  
  
You need to make sure that the AKS cluster is integrated with Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
Which manifest property should you change?
questions.explanation:
For legacy AKS Azure AD integration, the server application must be configured to emit group membership claims, typically by setting `groupMembershipClaims` to `All`. This setting controls the `groups` claim in issued tokens, which AKS uses for Azure AD group-based authorization.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra app manifest (Azure AD Graph format)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/reference-app-manifest) · [Azure Kubernetes Service integration with Microsoft Entra ID (legacy)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/azure-ad-integration-cli)

You strongly suspect that some users are attempting to sign in to resources they cannot access.  
  
You decide to create an Azure Log Analytics query to validate this suspicion. The query will identify unsuccessful user sign-in attempts from the past few days.  
  
You want to ensure the results show only users who have failed to sign in more than five times. Which of the following should be included in your query?
questions.explanation:
Windows failed logons are represented by SecurityEvent EventID 4625. A query should filter on that EventID, aggregate the matching events per user with `count()`, and retain counts greater than five. Microsoft’s SecurityEvent query examples use `EventID == 4625` with `summarize count()` to count failed logons by account.

**Learn more:** [Example log table queries for SecurityEvent - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/queries/securityevent)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure SQL database named `sql1`.  
  
You plan to audit `sql1`.  
  
You need to configure the destination for the audit logs. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Support querying events by using the Kusto query language.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace stores Azure SQL audit events in Azure Monitor Logs, where they can be queried directly by using Kusto Query Language (KQL). It provides managed log collection and analysis without needing a separate event consumer or processing pipeline.

**Learn more:** [Use Auditing to analyze audit logs and reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/auditing-analyze-audit-logs?view=azuresql-db) · [Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-platform-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant and a user named User1.  
  
The tenant's **App registrations** settings are configured as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953193151-ww4if3rm.jpg)  
  
You plan to deploy an app named App1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can register App1 in Azure AD. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to User1?

options.text: App Configuration Data Owner for the subscription
Managed Application Contributor for the subscription
Cloud application administrator in Azure AD

questions.explanation:
When the **Users can register applications** setting is set to **No**, assigning the Microsoft Entra **Application Developer** role restores the ability to create application registrations for that user. It grants only the app-registration capability needed, whereas Cloud Application Administrator grants broader application-management permissions; subscription-level roles do not provide this Microsoft Entra directory permission.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have the Azure virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783951828671-6k38ejyi.png)  
  
You create an Azure Log Analytics workspace named Analytics1 in RG1 in the East US region.  
  
Which virtual machines can be enrolled in Analytics1?
questions.explanation:
Azure virtual machines can send monitoring data to a Log Analytics workspace regardless of whether their resource group matches the workspace's resource group. A workspace can collect data from Azure resources and applications, and the listed Windows Server and Red Hat Enterprise Linux virtual machines can be connected to it; neither the differing resource groups nor the West Europe location prevents enrollment.

**Learn more:** [Collect log data from virtual machines with Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection) · [Create a Log Analytics workspace](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/quick-create-workspace)

options.text: a custom RBAC role for RG2
the Network Contributor role for RG2
the Contributor role for the subscription
a custom RBAC role for the subscription
the Network Contributor role for RG1
the Virtual Machine Contributor role for RG1

questions.explanation:
Assign Virtual Machine Contributor at the RG1 scope to allow virtual-machine creation and management only in that resource group. Assign a custom role at the RG2 scope that grants only the required virtual-network and subnet read/join actions, such as `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/read`, `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/read`, and `Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets/join/action`. Network Contributor is not least privilege because it grants `Microsoft.Network/*`, which permits broad network management.

**Learn more:** [Azure custom roles - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles) · [Azure built-in roles for Compute - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/compute)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1.  
  
You deploy a Linux virtual machine named VM1 in Subscription1.  
  
You need to monitor VM1's metrics and logs.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Linux Diagnostic Extension (LAD) 3.0 collects system performance metrics and syslog or specified log-file events from Azure Linux virtual machines, enabling monitoring of both required data types.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Linux diagnostic extension 3.0 to monitor metrics and logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/diagnostics-linux-v3)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
A partner company has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
You need to ensure that, when a user in fabrikam.com tries to access resources in contoso.com, the user receives only one Microsoft Entra Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) prompt. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the inbound access default settings.
From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the External collaboration settings.
From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the outbound access default settings.
From the Azure portal of fabrikam.com, configure the outbound access default settings.

questions.explanation:
Cross-tenant MFA trust is configured in the resource tenant's inbound cross-tenant access settings. When contoso trusts MFA claims from external Microsoft Entra tenants, it can accept MFA performed in fabrikam instead of requiring another MFA challenge. Configuring the inbound default settings provides this behavior with minimal administration.

**Learn more:** [Manage cross-tenant access settings for B2B collaboration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/cross-tenant-access-settings-b2b-collaboration)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM) resource named EASM1. EASM1 has discovery enabled and includes several inventory assets.  
  
You need to determine which inventory assets are vulnerable to the most critical web application security risks.  
  
Which Defender EASM dashboard should you use?
questions.explanation:
The OWASP Top 10 dashboard identifies assets with exposure to OWASP’s most critical web application security risks and provides remediation information for those risks.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understand dashboards in Microsoft Defender EASM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/external-attack-surface-management/understanding-dashboards)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM) resource named EASM1. EASM1 has discovery enabled and includes several inventory assets.  
  
You need to determine which inventory assets are vulnerable to the most critical web application security risks.  
  
Which Defender EASM dashboard should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Enable MFA security control has a maximum score of 10 points. Protecting all five subscription Owners with MFA earns 5 points, and protecting five of the ten Azure-resource Owners earns half of the remaining 5 points, or 2.5 points. The total Secure Score increase is therefore 7.5 points. Microsoft documents that a control’s score is based on the score per resource multiplied by the number of healthy resources, and that Enable MFA has a maximum score of 10.

**Learn more:** [Secure score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/secure-score-security-controls)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription associated with an Azure AD tenant named contoso.com. Contoso.com includes a user named User1 and an Azure web app named App1.  
  
You plan to allow User1 to perform these tasks:  
  
- Configure contoso.com to use Microsoft Entra Verified ID.  
- Register App1 in contoso.com.  
  
You need to determine which roles to assign to User1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two roles should you identify? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
questions.explanation:
The Authentication Policy Administrator role is required to configure a directory for Microsoft Entra Verified ID. The Application Administrator role can create and manage application registrations, including registering App1. Together, these roles grant the required capabilities without using broader directory-administration privileges.

**Learn more:** [Quick Microsoft Entra Verified ID setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/verified-id/verifiable-credentials-configure-tenant-quick) · [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 includes the subnets shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966701021-1m5t8ejp.png)  
  
You create the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966704479-aziwd3zl.png)  
  
You plan to configure just-in-time (JIT) VM access for the virtual machines. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
For which virtual machines can JIT VM access be configured?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access requires a network security group (NSG) or an Azure Firewall configuration. An NSG can be associated with either the VM's subnet or its network interface. Therefore, VM1, VM2, and VM3 are eligible because each is protected by an NSG at one or both of those scopes; VM4 has no NSG at either scope.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription and the computers displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960423143-7rizyqba.png)  
  
You need to run a vulnerability scan of the computers by using Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
Which computers can you scan?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud's integrated vulnerability assessment supports eligible Azure virtual machines and connected hybrid machines, including the listed Windows Server and RHEL machines. Under the scanner support scope used here, a virtual machine scale-set instance cannot be scanned through this vulnerability-assessment deployment, so VMSS1_0 is excluded.

**Learn more:** [Use Defender for Cloud vulnerability scanning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/auto-deploy-vulnerability-assessment) · [Apply Zero Trust principles to Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/azure-infrastructure-virtual-machines)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783952090205-noazmvh1.png)  
  
You need to ensure that the virtual machines in RG1 keep the Remote Desktop port closed until an authorized user requests access.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) conditional access

questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud blocks inbound traffic to selected VM management ports, including RDP, by default. When an authorized user requests access, it temporarily allows the configured port from the requested source IP address for a limited duration, then restores the block.

**Learn more:** [Just-in-time machine access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview) · [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
An Amazon Web Services (AWS) account named AWS1 is connected to Defender for Cloud.  
  
You need to ensure that AWS1 uses AWS Foundational Security Best Practices while minimizing administrative effort.  
  
What should you do in Defender for Cloud?
questions.explanation:
AWS Foundational Security Best Practices is a built-in Defender for Cloud compliance standard for AWS. Assigning that standard applies its collection of controls and assessments to the AWS account, avoiding the administrative work of defining custom standards or individual custom assessments.

**Learn more:** [Regulatory compliance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Determine multicloud security compliance requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/plan-multicloud-security-determine-compliance-requirements)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1 and a storage account that hosts a blob container named blob1.  
  
You must grant User1 access to blob1. The solution must ensure that the access expires after six days.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
A shared access signature (SAS) delegates limited access to an Azure Storage resource for a specified time interval. A SAS for the blob container can therefore grant the required permissions and be assigned an expiry time six days after it is issued.

**Learn more:** [Grant limited access to Azure Storage resources using shared access signatures (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview) · [Delegate access by using a shared access signature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/delegate-access-with-shared-access-signature)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a web app named App1.  
  
Users must be able to choose either a Google identity or a Microsoft identity when they authenticate to App1.  
  
You need to add Google as an identity provider in Azure AD.  
  
Which two pieces of information should you configure? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the endpoint URL of an application

questions.explanation:
Google federation in Microsoft Entra ID requires the OAuth client ID and client secret obtained when the Google application is registered. These credentials identify and authenticate the Entra tenant to Google.\
\
**Learn more:** [Google identity provider - Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/google-federation)

questions.question:
You are configuring connectivity for two Azure virtual networks, VNET1 and VNET2.  
  
Implement VPN gateways that meet these requirements:  
  
- VNET1 must support six site-to-site connections using BGP.  
- VNET2 must support 12 site-to-site connections using BGP.  
- Costs must be minimized.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 has a single subnet. The subscription also contains a virtual machine named VM1 that is connected to VNet1.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure SQL Managed Instance named SQL1.

Which three components must you create? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.

questions.explanation:
Azure SQL Managed Instance must use a dedicated subnet that contains no other resources, so VM1 cannot share its existing subnet with SQL1. questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Key Vault Standard key vault named Vault1. Vault1 contains a 2048-bit RSA key named key1.  
  
You need to ensure that key1 rotates every 90 days.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the Access policies settings of Vault1.
Upgrade Vault1 to Key Vault Premium.
Recreate key1 as an EC key.

questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault key autorotation is configured per key by creating or setting a key rotation policy. The policy can specify a rotation interval of 90 days, which creates a new version of the existing RSA key. Key Vault Standard supports this capability; neither a Premium upgrade nor changing the key type is required. Managing the policy requires appropriate permissions, but modifying access policies alone does not configure rotation.

**Learn more:** [Configure cryptographic key auto-rotation in Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/how-to-configure-key-rotation) · [az keyvault key rotation-policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/keyvault/key/rotation-policy?view=azure-cli-latest)

questions.question:
You are securing access to resources in an Azure subscription.  
  
A new company policy requires that every Azure virtual machine in the subscription use managed disks.  
  
You need to stop users from creating virtual machines that use unmanaged disks.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy enforces organizational standards at the subscription scope. A policy assignment with a Deny effect can reject virtual machine deployments that do not meet the managed-disk requirement, preventing unmanaged-disk VMs from being created.\

You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure key vault.  
  
You need to set the maximum number of days that newly created keys can remain valid. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Policy provides the built-in **Keys should have the specified maximum validity period** policy. Assigning it with the required maximum number of days governs Key Vault keys at the selected scope and can audit or deny noncompliant keys, avoiding manual per-key administration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Integrate Azure Key Vault with Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/azure-policy) · [Built-in policy definitions for Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/policy-reference)

You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure key vault.  
  
You need to set the maximum number of days that newly created keys can remain valid. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Just-in-time VM access requires an NSG or Azure Firewall configuration because it controls inbound management access by managing network rules. An NSG can apply at either the subnet or network-interface level. VM1 and VM3 are covered by the NSG associated with Subnet1, and VM4 is covered by the NSG associated with its network adapter. VM2 has neither a subnet-level nor network-adapter-level NSG, so it is not protected by JIT.

**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access) · [Just-in-time machine access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/just-in-time-access-overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You use Azure Resource Manager templates to deploy Azure virtual machines.  
  
You have been tasked with ensuring that unused Windows features are automatically disabled when virtual-machine instances are provisioned.  
  
Which of the following actions should you take?

options.text: You should make use of Azure DevOps.
You should make use of Azure Automation State Configuration.
You should make use of network security groups (NSG).
You should make use of Azure Blueprints.

questions.explanation:
Azure Automation State Configuration applies PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) to Azure VMs and maintains the specified configuration over time. A DSC `WindowsFeature` resource can set an unused Windows feature to `Ensure = 'Absent'`, automatically enforcing that feature’s disabled state.

**Learn more:** [Get started with Azure Automation State Configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-getting-started) · [Azure Automation State Configuration overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/automation/automation-dsc-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant and a root management group. You created 10 Azure subscriptions and added them to the root management group.  
  
You need to create an Azure Blueprints definition that will be stored in the root management group.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Modify the role-based access control (RBAC) role assignments for the root management group.
Add an Azure Policy definition to the root management group.

questions.explanation:
Azure RBAC permissions are separate from Azure AD directory roles, so having Global Administrator rights in Azure AD does not automatically grant permission to manage resources, such as Blueprint definitions, at the management group scope. To author and save a Blueprint definition in the root management group, the account must first be granted an appropriate RBAC role (such as Owner or Blueprint Contributor) at that management group scope. Therefore, the necessary first step is to modify the RBAC role assignments on the root management group so the required permissions are in place before the Blueprint definition can be created there.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Blueprints - Azure Blueprints | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/overview) · [How can I assign RBAC roles on the Tenant Root Management Group? - Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/957054/how-can-i-assign-rbac-roles-on-the-tenant-root-man)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a web app hosted on an on-premises server and accessed by using the URL `https://www.contoso.com`.  
  
You plan to migrate the web app to Azure and will continue using `https://www.contoso.com`.  
  
You need to enable HTTPS for the Azure web app.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Export the public key from the on-premises server and save the key as a P7b file.
Export the private key from the on-premises server and save the key as a PFX file that is encrypted by using TripleDES.
Export the public key from the on-premises server and save the key as a CER file.
Export the private key from the on-premises server and save the key as a PFX file that is encrypted by using AES256.

questions.explanation:
An Azure App Service TLS/SSL binding requires a PFX certificate that includes the private key; public-key-only CER and P7B files cannot establish the server’s HTTPS identity. For the required PFX compatibility, export the certificate with its private key using TripleDES encryption. Microsoft’s App Service documentation notes that PFX files using AES256 can require overriding the cipher to use 3DES for App Service support.

**Learn more:** [Install a TLS/SSL certificate for your app in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Files share named share1 and a user named User1. Identity-based authentication is configured for share1.  
  
User1 tries to access share1 from a Windows 10 device by using SMB.  
  
Which type of token does Azure Files use to authorize the request?
questions.explanation:
Azure Files uses Kerberos for identity-based authentication over SMB. The SMB client presents a Kerberos service ticket, which Azure Files uses to authorize access according to the configured share-level permissions and Windows ACLs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Files identity-based authentication for SMB access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/files/storage-files-active-directory-overview)

User1 tries to access share1 from a Windows 10 device by using SMB.  
  
Which type of token does Azure Files use to authorize the request?

options.text: only the display name of each user
only the user principal name (UPN) of each user
only the user principal name (UPN) and display name of each user
only the user principal name (UPN) and object identifier of each user
only the object identifier of each user

questions.explanation:
For bulk addition of users to an Azure AD administrative unit, the CSV template identifies each user by a user principal name (UPN), with one UPN entered per row. Display names are not identifiers for this operation, and the file does not require a paired object identifier.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957438882-zv3chxej.png)  
  
You need to configure **storage1** so that its keys are regenerated automatically every 90 days.  
  
Which cmdlet should you run?
questions.explanation:
`Add-AzKeyVaultManagedStorageAccount` adds an existing storage account to Azure Key Vault for Key Vault-managed storage keys. Its `-RegenerationPeriod` parameter sets the interval after which the inactive key is regenerated and made active; a 90-day `TimeSpan` configures automatic 90-day rotation. Storage account management policies apply to data lifecycle management rather than access-key regeneration.

**Learn more:** [Add-AzKeyVaultManagedStorageAccount (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/add-azkeyvaultmanagedstorageaccount?view=azps-15.3.0)

You create an MDM Security Baseline profile named Profile1.  
  
You need to identify the virtual machines to which Profile1 can be applied.  
  
Which virtual machines should you identify?

Microsoft’s MDM security baseline is designed for Windows client devices, including Windows 10 and later. Windows Server 2016, Windows Server 2019, and Ubuntu Server 18.04 LTS are not targets for this baseline, so only the Windows 10 virtual machine qualifies.

**Learn more:** [Mobile Device Management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm-overview) · [Learn about Intune security baselines for Windows devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/security-baselines/overview)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953053739-3seza5on.png)  
  
You need to ensure that VM1 can securely access a database on SQL1 by using a contained database user.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Enable a managed identity on VM1.
Configure a service endpoint on SQL1.

questions.explanation:
A managed identity gives VM1 a Microsoft Entra identity that can authenticate to Azure SQL without application-managed credentials. Azure SQL supports creating a contained database user for a managed identity by using `CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER`, after which the necessary database permissions can be granted.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Entra Authentication - Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-configure?view=azuresql) · [How managed identities work with Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-managed-identities-work-vm)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a web app named App1. App1 delivers product images and videos to users. Users reach App1 by using the URL `HTTPS://app1.contoso.com`.  
  
You deploy two server pools named Pool1 and Pool2. Pool1 hosts product images, and Pool2 hosts product videos.  
  
You need to optimize App1 performance. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Minimize the performance effect of TLS connections on Pool1 and Pool2.  
- Route user requests to the server pools according to the requested URL path.  
  
What should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Azure Front Door offloads client TLS connections at its edge points of presence and applies route rules that match URL paths, forwarding each request to the appropriate origin group. This reduces TLS-processing work on the image and video server pools while enabling path-based routing.

**Learn more:** [TLS encryption with Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/end-to-end-tls) · [How requests get matched to a route configuration - Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/front-door-route-matching)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that contains the resources shown in the following table.

You need to determine which initiatives and policies can be added to Subscription1 by using Azure Security Center.  
  
What should you identify?
questions.explanation:
Azure Security Center supports onboarding custom Azure Policy initiative definitions, which are collections of policy definitions. Standalone policy definitions cannot be added directly through the custom-initiative experience, and the initiative category is metadata rather than an eligibility restriction. Therefore, both initiative definitions can be added.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have been tasked with enabling Advanced Threat Protection for an Azure SQL Database server.  
  
Advanced Threat Protection must be configured to identify all threat-detection types.  
  
Which of the following occurs when an application generates a faulty SQL statement in the database?

options.text: A Potential SQL injection alert is triggered.
A Vulnerability to SQL injection alert is triggered.
An Access from a potentially harmful application alert is triggered.
A Brute force SQL credentials alert is triggered.

questions.explanation:
A faulty SQL statement generated by an application indicates a possible SQL-injection vulnerability, commonly caused by defective query construction or unsanitized input. Microsoft Defender for SQL classifies this condition as a vulnerability-to-SQL-injection alert; a potential SQL-injection alert instead indicates an active attempt to exploit an identified vulnerable application.

**Learn more:** [Alerts for SQL Database and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-sql-database-and-azure-synapse-analytics)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a resource group named RG1 and the identities shown in the following table.

You assign the Contributor role for RG1 to Group4.  
  
Which identities can be added as members of Group4?
questions.explanation:
Group4 is a role-assignable Microsoft Entra security group because Azure AD roles can be assigned to it. Group nesting is not supported for role-assignable groups, so Group1, Group2, and Group3 cannot be added to Group4. A user can be a member of the group; therefore, only User1 can be added.

**Learn more:** [Use Microsoft Entra groups to manage role assignments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/groups-concept) · [How to manage groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-to-manage-groups)

Azure Monitor Agent and Log Analytics agent are not used to establish this AWS integration; the Log Analytics agent is retired for Defender for Servers.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a resource group named RG1 and the network security groups (NSGs) shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960399249-lc0pn5d7.png)  
  
You create and assign the Azure Policy shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783960407345-azkrhi4i.png)  
  
What will the flow log status be for NSG1 and NSG2 after the Azure Policy is assigned?

options.text: Flow logs will be enabled for NSG1 only.
Flow logs will be enabled for NSG2 only.
Flow logs will be enabled for NSG1 and NSG2.
Flow logs will be disabled for NSG1 and NSG2.

questions.explanation:
NSG1 is excluded from the assignment scope and is not evaluated by the policy. NSG2 is evaluated, but the Audit effect only records noncompliance and does not alter resource configuration or create a remediation deployment. Therefore, neither NSG has its flow logs enabled, and both remain disabled.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions audit effect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-audit) · [What is applicability in Azure Policy?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/policy-applicability)
