questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company's Azure subscription contains an Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
Your company has one hundred on-premises servers running either Windows Server 2012 R2 or Windows Server 2016 that are connected to the Azure Log Analytics workspace. The workspace is configured to collect security-related performance counters from these connected servers.  
  
You are responsible for configuring alerts based on the information collected by the Azure Log Analytics workspace.  
  
You must ensure that alert rules support dimensions and that alert-creation time is minimized. In addition, a single alert notification must be generated when the alert is created and when it is resolved.  
  
You need to use the required signal type when creating the alert rules.  
  
Which of the following options should you use?

options.text: You should make use of the Activity log signal type.
You should make use of the Application Log signal type.
You should make use of the Metric signal type.
You should make use of the Audit Log signal type.

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor metric alert rules support dimensions, allowing monitoring of specific metric time series rather than only aggregated values. Metric alerts can be stateful, so they send a notification when the condition fires and a resolved notification when the condition clears. This makes the Metric signal type appropriate for performance-counter alerting with dimensional and resolution-notification requirements.

**Learn more:** [Create or edit a metric alert rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-metric-alert-rule) · [Overview of Azure Monitor alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-overview)

options.text: Configure the Azure AD tenant used by the new subscription to use pass-through authentication.
Configure the Azure AD tenant used by the new subscription to use federated authentication.
Change the Azure AD tenant used by the new subscription.
Configure a second instance of Azure AD Connect.

questions.explanation:
An Azure subscription trusts one Microsoft Entra ID tenant for authentication, authorization, and Azure RBAC identities. Associating the subscription with the Azure AD tenant that is synchronized with the on-premises Active Directory domain makes the synchronized user accounts available for Azure role assignments while retaining their Microsoft 365 directory identities. Pass-through authentication, federation, and another Azure AD Connect server do not change the tenant associated with the subscription.

**Learn more:** [Associate or add an Azure subscription to your Microsoft Entra tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-subscriptions-associated-directory)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud. The subscription includes an Azure Database for PostgreSQL instance.  
  
You need to make sure an email alert is triggered when a suspected brute-force attack against the database is detected. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: Microsoft Defender for open-source relational databases

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for open-source relational databases provides built-in threat detection for Azure Database for PostgreSQL, including suspected brute-force attacks, and raises Defender for Cloud alerts with email notifications. This avoids creating and maintaining custom monitoring logic or audit-based alerting.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Cloud for Azure Database for PostgreSQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/security/security-defender-for-cloud) · [Alerts for open-source relational databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/alerts-open-source-relational-databases)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a hybrid Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) configuration with Single Sign-On (SSO) enabled. An Azure SQL Database instance is configured to support Azure AD authentication.  
  
Database developers must connect to the database instance from a domain-joined device and authenticate by using their on-premises Active Directory account.  
  
You need to ensure that developers can connect to the instance by using Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio. The solution must minimize authentication prompts.  
  
Which authentication method should you recommend?

options.text: Active Directory - Universal with MFA support

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Integrated (formerly Active Directory - Integrated) authentication uses the signed-in Windows user's domain credentials in a hybrid identity environment. It supports single sign-on to Azure SQL Database from a domain-joined device, avoiding separate username/password entry and minimizing interactive authentication prompts.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Authentication - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/authentication-aad-overview?view=azuresql) · [SSMS: Connect and query data - Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/connect-query-ssms?view=azuresql-mi)

You have an Azure subscription that includes a managed identity named Identity1 and the Azure key vaults shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957436149-g05p4wbh.png)  
  
KeyVault1 has an access policy that grants Identity1 these key permissions:  
  
- Get  
- List  
- Wrap  
- Unwrap  
  
You need to grant Identity1 the same permissions for KeyVault2. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to Identity1?

options.text: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User

questions.explanation:
The **Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User** role allows reading key metadata and performing key wrap and unwrap operations in a vault that uses Azure RBAC. This corresponds to the Get, List, Wrap, and Unwrap key permissions while avoiding the additional cryptographic and key-management capabilities granted by broader roles. Microsoft’s access-policy-to-RBAC mapping specifically maps these permissions to this role.

**Learn more:** [Migrate to Azure role-based access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-migration) · [Azure built-in roles for Security - Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using federation with Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS).  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
AD FS federation authenticates users through the on-premises identity infrastructure, allowing Active Directory password and sign-in restrictions to be enforced. However, federation requires additional AD FS infrastructure and typically external-access proxy infrastructure, so it does not reduce the number of required servers.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect and federation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-fed-whatis) · [AD FS Password Attack protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/technical-reference/ad-fs-password-protection)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using pass-through authentication and seamless SSO together with password hash synchronization.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Pass-through authentication enforces on-premises Active Directory account policies at sign-in, including disabled or locked accounts, password expiration, and permitted sign-in hours. It can be combined with Seamless SSO, and password hash synchronization may be enabled for backup or supporting features while pass-through authentication remains the primary sign-in method. This avoids deploying a separate AD FS federation infrastructure.\
\
**Learn more:** [Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn) · [User sign-in with Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta)

questions.question:
Solution: You recommend using password hash synchronization and seamless SSO.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Password hash synchronization performs authentication in Microsoft Entra ID rather than against on-premises Active Directory. Seamless SSO only provides automatic sign-in for eligible corporate devices; it does not cause Active Directory user logon limitations to be evaluated for cloud authentication. Consequently, this configuration cannot ensure that both password policies and user logon limitations affect synchronized accounts.\
\
**Learn more:** [Implement password hash synchronization with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-password-hash-synchronization) · [Microsoft Entra seamless single sign-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sso)

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that uses Microsoft Entra Permissions Management and includes the accounts shown in the following table:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966710640-we6mo6zs.png)  
  
Which accounts are listed as assigned to highly privileged roles on the Azure AD insights tab in the Entra Permissions Management portal?
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Entra Insights tab reviews Global Administrator assignments separately. Its highly privileged-role review includes the Privileged Role Administrator and Exchange Administrator roles, so Admin2 and Admin4 are included. Privileged Authentication Administrator is not in that curated highly privileged-role list.

**Learn more:** [View privileged role assignments in Microsoft Entra Insights](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/entra/permissions-management/product-privileged-role-insights)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a resource group named RG1 and the network security groups (NSGs) shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957437267-ae13jak7.png)  
  
You create the Azure Policy shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957443479-876fskan.png)  
  
You assign the policy to RG1.  
  
What happens to NSG1 and NSG2 when the policy is assigned?

options.text: Flow logs will be enabled for NSG2 only.
Flow logs will be disabled for NSG1 and NSG2.
Flow logs will be enabled for NSG1 and NSG2.
Flow logs will be enabled for NSG1 only.

questions.explanation:
NSG1 is excluded from the policy assignment. NSG2 is evaluated, but an Azure Policy **Audit** effect only records noncompliance and does not change the resource configuration. It therefore cannot enable flow logs. Because flow logs are initially off for both NSGs, they remain disabled.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions audit effect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-audit) · [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview)

questions.question:
Your company uses Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to recommend a way to validate that code satisfies the company's quality and code-review standards.  
  
What should you recommend implementing in Azure DevOps?
questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps branch policies enforce code-quality and change-management standards on pull requests. They can require build validation and a minimum number of reviewer approvals before code can merge into a protected branch.\
\
**Learn more:** [Branch policies and settings — Azure Repos | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
Your company uses Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to recommend a way to validate that code satisfies the company's quality and code-review standards.  
  
What should you recommend implementing in Azure DevOps?
questions.explanation:
The `DeployIfNotExists` Azure Policy effect deploys a template when the required related resource does not exist, enabling the antimalware VM extension to be installed on VMs that lack it. Microsoft’s built-in policy that deploys the default IaaSAntimalware extension for Windows Server also uses `deployIfNotExists`.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deployIfNotExists effect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deploy-if-not-exists) · [Built-in policy definitions for Azure Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/policy-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953372594-w9biztw5.png)  
  
You plan to enable Azure Defender for the subscription. Which resources can Azure Defender protect?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud provides workload-protection plans for virtual machines (Defender for Servers), storage accounts (Defender for Storage), and Azure Key Vault (Defender for Key Vault). It does not provide an Azure Defender plan that protects a virtual network as a resource.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Cloud documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/) · [Overview of Microsoft Defender for Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-key-vault-introduction)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network has an on-premises Active Directory domain named corp.contoso.com.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is associated with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com. You synchronize all on-premises identities to Azure AD.  
  
You need to stop users whose `givenName` attribute begins with TEST from being synchronized to Azure AD. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Synchronization Rules Editor lets Azure AD Connect apply attribute-based scoping filters, including string-prefix conditions, and exclude matching user objects from synchronization by setting `cloudFiltered`. This centrally filters all users whose `givenName` starts with TEST without individually administering their AD accounts.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Configure filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-configure-filtering) · [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Make a change to the default configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-change-the-configuration)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains the Azure key vaults shown in the following table:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783952082479-ns67f5qh.png)  
  
In Sub1, you create a virtual machine with the following configuration:  
  
- Name: VM1  
- Size: DS2v2  
- Resource group: RG1  
- Region: West Europe  
- Operating system: Windows Server 2016  
  
You plan to enable Azure Disk Encryption on VM1.  
  
In which key vaults can you store VM1's encryption key?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption requires the key vault and virtual machine to reside in the same Azure region and subscription. VM1 is in West Europe in Sub1, so Vault1 and Vault3 qualify. A key vault may be in a different resource group; Vault2 and Vault4 are in East US and do not qualify.

**Learn more:** [Enable Azure Disk Encryption for Windows VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/disk-encryption-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that contains an Azure Policy definition called Policy1. Policy1 has these settings:  
  
- Definition location: Tenant Root Group  
- Category: Monitoring  
  
You need to ensure that resources noncompliant with Policy1 are displayed in the Azure Security Center dashboard.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Change the Category of Policy1 to Security Center.
Add Policy1 to a custom initiative.
Change the Definition location of Policy1 to Sub1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud/Azure Security Center uses Azure Policy initiatives as security standards for evaluating and presenting compliance. A custom policy definition must be added to a custom initiative before that initiative can be onboarded and assigned to the subscription so its noncompliant resources can appear in the security dashboard.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Regulatory Compliance in initiative definitions - Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/regulatory-compliance)

questions.question:
You have a web app named WebApp1.  
  
You create a web application firewall (WAF) policy named WAF1.  
  
You need to use WAF1 to protect WebApp1.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
Azure WAF policies take effect when associated with an application-delivery platform such as Azure Front Door. Deploying Azure Front Door provides the resource and domain association through which WAF1 can protect WebApp1; Azure Firewall and an app extension do not fulfill that WAF-policy association.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage Azure Web Application Firewall policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall-manager/manage-web-application-firewall-policies) · [What is Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/afds-overview)

questions.question:
You have the Azure virtual machines listed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953059031-kx5212q4.png)  
  
For which virtual machines can Update Management be enabled?
questions.explanation:
Update Management supports Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, Windows Server 2016, and Ubuntu Server 18.04 LTS. A stopped VM can be enabled for management, although update assessment and deployment require the VM to be running.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Update Manager support matrix for updates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/update-manager/support-matrix-updates?pivots=azure-vm&tabs=ci-win)

options.text: From container1, change the access level.
From container1, add an access policy.
From container1, modify the Access Control (IAM) settings.
From storage1, enable soft delete for blobs.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Blob Storage immutability policy enforces write-once, read-many (WORM) protection: while it is in effect, blobs can be read but cannot be modified or deleted. A container-level immutability policy is added through the container's Access policy pane.

**Learn more:** [Configure immutability policies for containers - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-policy-configure-container-scope) · [Store business-critical blob data with immutable storage in a write once, read many (WORM) state](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/immutable-storage-overview)

questions.question:
You intend to implement JIT VM access.  
  
Which virtual machines are supported?
questions.explanation:
For the historical JIT VM-access capability tested here, the supported machines are the Windows Server virtual machines: VM1 and VM3. The Linux virtual machines, VM2 and VM4, are outside that item’s supported operating-system scope.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable just-in-time access - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-just-in-time-access)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
You intend to implement JIT VM access.  
  
Which virtual machines are supported?
questions.explanation:
Azure Bastion can securely connect to VMs in the virtual network where it is deployed and to VMs in peered virtual networks. This support includes both same-region virtual network peering and global virtual network peering across Azure regions. Therefore, the host in VNET2 can protect VM2 locally, VM1 and VM3 in VNET1, and VM4 in VNET3.

**Learn more:** [Virtual network peering and Azure Bastion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/vnet-peering) · [Choose the right Azure Bastion SKU to meet your needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-sku-comparison)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Azure DevOps and has configured branch policies.  
  
Which statements about branch policies are **TRUE**? (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: It enforces your team's change management standards.
It controls who can read and update the code in a branch.
It enforces your team's code quality.
It places a branch into a read-only state.

questions.explanation:
Azure DevOps branch policies enforce a team’s change-management standards and code-quality requirements by requiring conditions such as pull-request reviews, successful builds, and status checks before changes can merge. Branch permissions—not policies—control who can read or update branch code. [Git branch policies and settings - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies?view=azure-devops)

**Learn more:** [Git branch policies and settings - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-policies?view=azure-devops) · [Set Git branch security and permissions - Azure Repos](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/repos/git/branch-permissions?view=azure-devops)

questions.question:
You need to determine which virtual machines should be used to host App1. The solution must satisfy the technical requirements for KeyVault1.  
  
Which virtual machines should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption requires the Azure Key Vault and the virtual machine to reside in the same Azure region and subscription. VM1 is the only eligible host; adding VM2, VM3, or VM4 would not satisfy the KeyVault1 placement constraint.\
\
**Learn more:** [Enable Azure Disk Encryption for Windows VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/disk-encryption-overview)

questions.question:

You need to create a scheduled query rule called Rule1.  
  
What should you use to define the query-rule logic for Rule1?

Microsoft Sentinel scheduled analytics rules run Kusto Query Language (KQL) queries against data in the Log Analytics workspace. The rule query contains the detection logic that is evaluated on the configured schedule.\

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure SQL Database logical server named SQL1 and an Azure virtual machine named VM1. VM1 uses only a private IP address.  
  
The Firewall and virtual networks settings for SQL1 are shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783957448570-80ga64em.png)

options.text: Set Allow Azure services and resources to access this server to Yes.

Adding VM1’s existing virtual network/subnet provides the required narrowly scoped access, typically using the Microsoft.Sql service endpoint. IP firewall rules require a public source IP, while allowing Azure services broadly permits Azure resources beyond VM1.

You have been tasked with delegating administrative access to your company's Azure key vault.  
  
You need to ensure that:  
  
- A specific user can set advanced access policies for the key vault.  
- Access is assigned based on the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which of the following options should you use to achieve your goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Key Vault management-plane operations, including configuring advanced access policies, are governed by Azure RBAC. By assigning the user an appropriate RBAC role (such as the built-in Key Vault Contributor role) scoped to just that key vault, you grant only the permissions needed to manage access policies, satisfying the principle of least privilege. Azure Information Protection handles data classification and labeling, not Key Vault access delegation; Azure AD PIM manages time-bound activation of already-granted roles rather than defining the access-policy permission itself; and Azure DevOps is unrelated to Key Vault permission management.

**Learn more:** [Assign a Key Vault access policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/assign-access-policy) · [Azure built-in roles for Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security#key-vault-contributor)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure SQL server named SQL1. SQL1 contains an Azure SQL database named DB1.  
  
You need to use Microsoft Defender for Cloud to perform a vulnerability assessment for DB1.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Advanced Threat Protection types, select SQL injection vulnerability.
Configure the Send scan report to setting.
Set Periodic recurring scans to ON.
Enable the Microsoft Defender for SQL plan.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Azure SQL must be enabled before vulnerability-assessment scans can run on Azure SQL databases. Enabling the Defender for SQL plan activates the required protection and vulnerability-assessment capability; recurring scans and scan-report settings can be configured afterward.

**Learn more:** [Enable vulnerability assessment on your Azure SQL databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/sql-azure-vulnerability-assessment-enable) · [Deploy Defender for Azure SQL Databases](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/enable-sql-database-plan)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant.  
  
You plan to deploy an authentication solution that meets the following requirements:  
  
- Require number matching.  
- Show the geographic location during sign-in.  
  
Which authentication method should you include in the solution?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Authenticator supports number matching for push notifications. Its additional-context settings can also show the geographic location of the sign-in in Authenticator push and passwordless notifications.\
\
**Learn more:** [How number matching works in MFA push notifications for Authenticator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-mfa-number-match) · [Use additional context in Authenticator notifications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-mfa-additional-context)

questions.question:
In Microsoft Defender for Cloud, you need to deploy SecPol1.  
  
What should you do first?
questions.explanation:
A Defender for Cloud security policy is based on an Azure Policy initiative, which bundles the policy definitions and controls that will be applied. The initiative must exist before it can be onboarded or assigned as a security standard.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create custom security standards and recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations)

questions.question:
You are configuring an Azure Policy through the Azure portal.  
  
Your policy will include an effect that requires a managed identity in order to be assigned.  
  
Which of the following is that effect?
questions.explanation:
The `DeployIfNotExists` effect deploys a template to remediate noncompliant resources. Azure Policy uses the managed identity associated with the policy assignment to perform that deployment, so this effect requires a managed identity.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deployIfNotExists effect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deploy-if-not-exists) · [Remediate non-compliant resources with Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/how-to/remediate-resources)

questions.question:
You are configuring an Azure Policy through the Azure portal.  
  
Your policy will include an effect that requires a managed identity in order to be assigned.  
  
Which of the following is that effect?

options.text: You will be able to start VirMac1.
You will NOT be able to start VirMac1.
You will be able to create a virtual machine in ResGroup2.
You will NOT be able to create a virtual machine in ResGroup2.

questions.explanation:
A Read-only Azure resource lock allows only read operations and blocks modifications. Starting or restarting a virtual machine is a control-plane POST operation, so the Read-only lock on VirMac1 prevents it from being started. A Read-only lock at the resource-group scope prevents resource creation within that group; therefore, no virtual machine can be created in ResGroup2. An Allowed resource types policy permits the specified type but does not override a resource lock.

**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources) · [Tutorial: Disallow resource types in your cloud environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/tutorials/disallowed-resources)

questions.question:
You have an Azure AD tenant that includes a user named User1.  
  
You purchase an app named App1.  
  
User1 must publish App1 by using Azure AD Application Proxy.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User1?
questions.explanation:
The Application Administrator role can create and manage enterprise applications, application registrations, and Application Proxy settings, including publishing applications through Application Proxy. The Cloud Application Administrator role excludes Application Proxy management.\
\
**Learn more:** [Delegate application management administrator permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/delegate-app-roles) · [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that contains a virtual network named VNet1. VNet1 contains the subnets shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966881733-m4zbf7c5.png)  
  
The subscription contains the function apps shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966886097-0k9kba4k.png)  
  
For which app is outbound traffic controlled by using NSG1?
questions.explanation:
Virtual network integration sends an app’s applicable outbound traffic through its integration subnet, where network security group rules apply. App1, App2, and App3 are integrated with Subnet1, Subnet2, and Subnet3, respectively; App4 is deployed to Subnet4 in the isolated tier. Because NSG1 is associated with each of those subnets, it controls the applicable outbound traffic of all four apps.

**Learn more:** [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration) · [App Service Environment networking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/environment/networking)

questions.question:

You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account.  
  
What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?
questions.explanation:
Azure Storage Analytics log data is stored as blobs. AzCopy can download the relevant log blobs from the storage account to retrieve them for analysis.\

questions.question:
Your company has recently created an Azure subscription.  
  
You have been tasked with ensuring that a specified user can implement Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Which of the following roles should you assign to the user?
questions.explanation:
A Global Administrator has the directory-wide administrative permissions needed to implement and manage Privileged Identity Management for Microsoft Entra roles. PIM role-assignment management is limited to Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators; of the listed roles, only Global Administrator qualifies.\

Manually add the Azure CIS 1.4.0 standard.

An available built-in standard is enabled from Manage compliance policies by locating the standard and turning it on; creating or assigning a separate policy or custom initiative adds unnecessary administration.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure virtual machine named VM1.  
  
From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, you receive the following high-severity recommendation: `Install endpoint protection solutions on virtual machine`.  
  
You need to resolve the issue that is triggering the high-severity recommendation.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add the Microsoft Antimalware extension to VM1.
Install Microsoft System Center Security Management Pack for Endpoint Protection on VM1.
Add the Network Watcher Agent for Windows extension to VM1.
Onboard VM1 to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.

questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Antimalware extension installs endpoint protection on an Azure virtual machine, satisfying the recommendation for a missing endpoint protection solution. Microsoft Learn identifies Microsoft Antimalware as an Azure VM extension used to provide antimalware protection, while network monitoring extensions and System Center management packs do not install endpoint protection.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Antimalware for Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/antimalware) · [Compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing three users: User1, User2, and User3.  
  
You configure Microsoft Entra Password Protection as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783966712655-gkfyokxi.png)  
  
The users perform these tasks:  
  
- User1 attempts to reset her password to `C0nt0s0`.  
- User2 attempts to reset her password to `F@brikamHQ`.  
- User3 attempts to reset her password to `Pr0duct123`.  
  
Which password-reset attempts fail?
questions.explanation:
With the custom banned-password list enforced, `Contoso`, `Fabrikam`, and `Product` are evaluated after normalizing common substitutions such as `0` to `o` and `@` to `a`. Each proposed password contains a configured banned term but has fewer than the five points required for acceptance after the banned term and remaining characters are scored. Therefore, all three password resets fail.

**Learn more:** [Eliminate bad passwords using Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-password-ban-bad) · [Configure custom banned passwords for Microsoft Entra password protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-configure-custom-password-protection)

questions.question:
Solution: Create a site-to-site VPN between the virtual network and the on-premises network.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
A site-to-site VPN provides connectivity but does not configure the supported Active Directory authentication environment for HDInsight. HDInsight Enterprise Security Package requires Microsoft Entra Domain Services; on-premises Active Directory identities must be synchronized through Microsoft Entra ID to that managed domain service.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Enterprise Security Package in HDInsight](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/domain-joined/apache-domain-joined-architecture)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy an On-premises data gateway to the on-premises network.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An on-premises data gateway provides connectivity to on-premises data sources; it does not synchronize Active Directory identities or provide the Microsoft Entra Domain Services and Kerberos authentication configuration required for HDInsight users to sign in with on-premises Active Directory credentials.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure HDInsight architecture with Enterprise Security Package](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/domain-joined/apache-domain-joined-architecture) · [On-premises data gateway architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/data-integration/gateway/service-gateway-onprem-indepth)

questions.domain: Secure Azure using Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel
questions.question:
Solution: You deploy Azure Active Directory Domain Services (Azure AD DS) to the Azure subscription.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
HDInsight Enterprise Security Package integrates with Microsoft Entra Domain Services to provide Active Directory-based authentication. This allows enterprise users to authenticate to the cluster with their domain credentials in a hybrid identity environment.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of enterprise security in Azure HDInsight](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/domain-joined/hdinsight-security-overview) · [Create and configure Enterprise Security Package clusters in Azure HDInsight](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/domain-joined/apache-domain-joined-create-configure-enterprise-security-cluster)

questions.question:
Solution: You deploy an Azure AD Application Proxy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure AD Application Proxy provides remote access to on-premises applications through Microsoft Entra ID, not Active Directory domain services for HDInsight. HDInsight authentication with on-premises Active Directory credentials requires Microsoft Entra Domain Services integration, with synchronized identities as appropriate.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use Enterprise Security Package in HDInsight](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/hdinsight/domain-joined/apache-domain-joined-architecture) · [Add an on-premises application for remote access through application proxy in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/app-proxy/application-proxy-add-on-premises-application)

questions.question:
You need to collect logs from many Windows Server 2016 computers by using Azure Log Analytics.  
  
You are configuring an Azure Resource Manager template to automatically deploy the Microsoft Monitoring Agent to every server. Which of the following must be included in the template? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation:
The Microsoft Monitoring Agent extension connects to a Log Analytics workspace by using the workspace ID in its settings and the workspace key in protected settings. Azure AD application IDs and Storage account keys are not part of this agent extension configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Resource Manager template samples for agents in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/agents/resource-manager-agent)

questions.question:

You are configuring an Azure Resource Manager template to automatically deploy the Microsoft Monitoring Agent to every server. Which of the following must be included in the template? (Choose all that apply.)
questions.explanation:
The Privileged Role Administrator role can create and manage role-assignable groups, assign Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) roles to groups, and create access reviews for membership in role-assignable groups. Groups Administrator lacks the required privileged role-management capabilities, while the other listed roles do not provide the complete set of permissions.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Create a role-assignable group in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/groups-create-eligible)

You enable Azure Storage Analytics logs and archive them to a storage account. What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?

Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Antimalware for Azure is deployed to supported Windows Server 2012 R2 virtual machines through the Azure VM Antimalware extension. Windows Defender is built into Windows Server 2016, but installing a Windows feature on each guest does not deploy the required Azure antimalware protection to the Windows Server 2012 R2 virtual machines.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Antimalware Extension for Windows VMs on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/iaas-antimalware-windows)

questions.question:
Solution: You add an extension to every virtual machine.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
The Azure VM Antimalware extension enables and configures Microsoft Antimalware on supported Windows virtual machines. Windows Server 2012 R2 is supported, and on Windows Server 2016 the extension configures the built-in Windows Defender antimalware protection.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Antimalware Extension for Windows VMs on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/extensions/iaas-antimalware-windows)

You enable diagnostic logs for the storage account.  
  
What should you use to retrieve the diagnostic logs?

**Learn more:** [Enable and manage Azure Storage Analytics logs (classic)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/manage-storage-analytics-logs)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) in a hybrid configuration. Every user uses hybrid Azure AD joined Windows 10 computers.  
  
You administer an Azure SQL database that supports Azure AD authentication.  
  
You need to ensure database developers can connect to the SQL database through Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS). You must also ensure that the developers authenticate by using their on-premises Active Directory account. Your strategy should keep authentication prompts to a minimum.

Hybrid joining the on-premises AD environment enables single sign-on to Azure SQL, so developers can use their on-premises AD accounts without repeated credential prompts.

You need to onboard VM1 to Microsoft Defender for Cloud by using Azure Arc.  
  
What should you install first?
questions.explanation:
The Azure Connected Machine agent registers an on-premises or other non-Azure virtual machine with Azure Arc as an Arc-enabled server. This Azure Arc connection is the prerequisite for onboarding the machine to Microsoft Defender for Cloud through Azure Arc.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Arc-enabled servers overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/overview) · [Overview of the Azure Connected Machine agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/agent-overview)

You need to onboard VM1 to Microsoft Defender for Cloud by using Azure Arc.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You have accounts for these cloud services:  
  
- Alibaba Cloud  
- Amazon Web Services (AWS)  
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP)  
  
What can you add to Defender for Cloud?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud can onboard Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects through its multicloud security connectors. Alibaba Cloud is not supported by these Defender for Cloud connectors.

**Learn more:** [Connect hybrid and multicloud environments to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/connect-hybrid-multicloud-environments-defender/) · [Connect AWS accounts to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws)

questions.question:
You need to encrypt `storage1` to satisfy the technical requirements.  
  
Which key vaults can you use?
questions.explanation:
KeyVault1 is the only vault that satisfies the case-study requirements for encrypting Storage1 with customer-managed keys. Azure Storage customer-managed keys must be held in an eligible Azure Key Vault configuration, including soft delete and purge protection; automatic use of new key versions is enabled by using a versionless key URI.\
\

questions.question:
Your company has an Azure Container Registry.  
  
You have been asked to assign a user a role that permits downloading images from the Azure Container Registry. The assigned role must not grant more privileges than necessary.  
  
Which of the following roles should you assign?
questions.explanation:
The `AcrPull` role grants permission to pull (download) images and artifacts from an Azure Container Registry without granting push, delete, or registry-management permissions. It is the least-privilege built-in role for this access requirement.\
\

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription that includes the resources shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783954793927-lcuwzg1c.png)  
  
You plan to deploy the virtual machines shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783954798892-bc5a8x5l.png)  
  
You must assign managed identities to the virtual machines. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Assign every virtual machine its required roles.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
What is the minimum number of managed identities required?
questions.explanation:
A user-assigned managed identity can be shared across multiple Azure resources. One identity can have Storage Blob Data Reader on storage1 and Key Vault Reader on Vault1 for VM1 and VM2. A second identity can have those roles plus Key Vault Reader on Vault2 for VM3 and VM4. A single shared identity would give VM1 and VM2 unnecessary access to Vault2, which violates least privilege.

**Learn more:** [How managed identities for Azure resources work with Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-managed-identities-work-vm) · [Best practice recommendations for managed system identities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/managed-identity-best-practice-recommendations)

options.text: An Azure Sentinel scheduled query rule is executed.

questions.explanation:

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription containing a storage account and an Azure web app named App1.  
  
App1 connects to an Azure Cosmos DB database named Cosmos1 that uses a private endpoint named Endpoint1. Endpoint1 uses the default settings.  
  
You need to verify name resolution for Cosmos1.  
  
Which DNS zone should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Cosmos DB private endpoints for the default SQL/NoSQL subresource use the `privatelink.documents.azure.com` private DNS namespace. Therefore, the matching Endpoint1 DNS entry is `endpoint1.privatelink.documents.azure.com`.

- Region: West US  
- Virtual network: VNet1

- Region: West US  
- VNet integration: Enabled  
- Windows plan (West US): ASP1  
  
To which subnets can WebApp2 be integrated?
questions.explanation:
An App Service plan can have virtual network integrations with up to two subnets or virtual networks, while multiple apps in that plan can share the same integration. Your company’s Azure subscription contains one hundred virtual machines with Azure Diagnostics enabled.  
  
You must retrieve the identity of the user who removed a virtual machine 15 days ago. You have already opened Azure Monitor.

questions.explanation:

options.text: In Azure AD, create a role.

questions.explanation:

questions.explanation:

options.text: From the Roles and administrators blade, assign the Security administrator role to Admin1.
From the Organizational relationships blade, add an identity provider.
From the Custom domain names blade, add a custom domain.
From the Users blade, modify the External collaboration settings.

questions.explanation:
External collaboration settings control which users and administrator roles may invite B2B guest users. A User Administrator can invite guests when the guest invite policy allows that role; therefore, adjusting the external collaboration settings removes a tenant invitation restriction that causes the authorization failure.

**Learn more:** [Configure external collaboration settings for B2B in Microsoft Entra External ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/external-collaboration-settings-configure) · [Troubleshoot B2B issues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/troubleshoot)

questions.explanation:

You have an Azure subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can create managed identities. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a management group and assign User1 the Hybrid Identity Administrator Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) role.
Create a management group and assign User1 the Managed Identity Operator role.
Create a resource group and assign User1 to the Managed Identity Contributor role.
Create an organizational unit (OU) and assign User1 the User administrator Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) role.

questions.explanation:
The Managed Identity Contributor role grants permission to create user-assigned managed identities, including `Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/write`. Assigning it at the resource-group scope confines that capability to the resources in that group, satisfying least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in roles for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/identity) · [Manage user-assigned managed identities using the Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/manage-user-assigned-managed-identities-azure-cli)

questions.question:
An Azure virtual machine runs Windows Server R2.  
  
You plan to deploy and configure an Azure Key Vault, then enable Azure Disk Encryption for the virtual machine.  
  
Which of the following statements is **TRUE** regarding Azure Disk Encryption for a Windows VM?

options.text: It is supported for basic tier VMs.
It is supported for standard tier VMs.
It is supported for VMs configured with software-based RAID systems.
It is supported for VMs configured with Storage Spaces Direct (S2D).

questions.explanation:
Azure Disk Encryption for Windows VMs is unavailable for Basic-tier VMs, software-based RAID configurations, and Storage Spaces Direct (S2D). Standard-tier VMs are supported, provided the VM also meets the applicable operating system, size, and configuration requirements.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Disk Encryption scenarios on Windows VMs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/disk-encryption-windows)

Your company intends to create separate subscriptions for every department. Each subscription will be associated with the same Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You need to configure every subscription with identical role assignments.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blueprints supports role-assignment artifacts and can apply a reusable blueprint to subscriptions, providing consistent Azure RBAC role assignments across them.\
\
**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Blueprints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/overview)

questions.question:
Your company intends to create separate subscriptions for every department. Each subscription will be associated with the same Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
You need to configure every subscription with identical role assignments.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Roles are being assigned outside of Privileged Identity Management
Roles don't require multi-factor authentication for activation
Administrators aren't using their privileged roles
Potential stale accounts in a privileged role

questions.explanation:
The "Potential stale accounts in a privileged role" alert in Azure AD PIM checks whether privileged accounts have changed their password or signed in within a configurable number of days, with a default threshold of 90 days. Because the company's password rotation policy is 180 days, accounts that are fully compliant with the 180-day policy still trigger this alert under its default 90-day setting. To reduce the number of alerts without violating the security policy, you adjust the threshold configuration of this specific alert to match the organization's 180-day password change requirement, rather than modifying alerts related to MFA enforcement, role assignment outside PIM, or role usage.

**Learn more:** [Azure AD Privileged Identity Management security alerts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-how-to-configure-security-alerts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory forest named contoso.com and an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant also named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to configure synchronization by using the **Express Settings** installation option in Azure AD Connect.  
  
You need to determine which roles and groups are required to perform the planned configuration. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which two roles and groups should you identify? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: the Domain Admins group in Active Directory
the Security administrator role in Azure AD
the Global administrator role in Azure AD
the User administrator role in Azure AD
the Enterprise Admins group in Active Directory

questions.explanation:
Azure AD Connect Express Settings requires a tenant administrative account and an on-premises AD DS Enterprise Administrator account. Enterprise Admins provides the forest-wide rights Express Settings needs to configure Active Directory permissions across domains. Among the listed Azure AD roles, Global administrator supplies the required tenant-level administrative access; Security administrator and User administrator do not.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect: Accounts and permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/reference-connect-accounts-permissions) · [Install your synchronization tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/install)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network includes an Active Directory forest named contoso.com. The forest has one domain.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is associated with an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure AD Connect and integrate Active Directory with the Azure AD tenant.  
  
You need to recommend an integration solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Ensures that password policies and user logon restrictions apply to user accounts synchronized to the tenant  
- Minimizes the number of servers required for the solution  
  
Which authentication method should you include in the recommendation?

options.text: federated identity with Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS)
password hash synchronization with seamless single sign-on (SSO)
pass-through authentication with seamless single sign-on (SSO)

questions.explanation:
Pass-through authentication validates credentials directly against on-premises Active Directory at sign-in, enforcing on-premises account policies such as password expiration, account lockout, disabled accounts, and permitted sign-in hours. It uses lightweight authentication agents and requires substantially less on-premises infrastructure than an AD FS federation deployment.

**Learn more:** [Choose the right authentication method for your Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn)

You have an Azure subscription containing the Azure Log Analytics workspaces shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953041830-8uwqgzhq.png)

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953044403-xbjdo0u0.png)  
  
You plan to use Azure Sentinel to monitor Windows Defender Firewall on the virtual machines.  
  
Which virtual machines can you connect to Azure Sentinel?
questions.explanation:
Windows Firewall logs can be forwarded to a SIEM such as Microsoft Sentinel through a Log Analytics workspace. Windows monitoring agents can send data to multiple Log Analytics workspaces, so an existing connection to Workspace2 does not prevent VM2 or VM4 from also sending firewall data to the Sentinel-enabled Workspace1. The virtual machines' East US or West US locations do not restrict this connection.

**Learn more:** [Collect Firewall logs with Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/vm/data-collection-firewall-logs) · [Design a Log Analytics workspace architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/workspace-design)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named Contoso.com and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster named AKS1.  
  
You find that AKS1 cannot be accessed by accounts from Contoso.com.  
  
You need to ensure that accounts from Contoso.com can access AKS1. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From AKS1, upgrade the version of Kubernetes.
From Microsoft Entra, add a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license.
From Microsoft Entra, configure the User settings.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra authentication for AKS relies on Microsoft Entra application registrations. The tenant’s User settings control whether non-administrative users can register applications, so configuring that setting is the appropriate low-effort prerequisite for enabling access with tenant accounts. A Kubernetes upgrade and a P2 license do not enable this authentication path, while recreating the cluster is unnecessary.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference) · [Use Kubernetes RBAC with Microsoft Entra ID in AKS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/kubernetes-rbac-entra-id)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are testing an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster. The cluster configuration is shown in the exhibit. (Click the Exhibit tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953213147-2x5eyc1h.png)  
  
You plan to deploy the cluster into production and disable HTTP application routing.  
  
You need to implement application routing that provides reverse-proxy functionality and TLS termination for AKS services by using a single IP address.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Install the container network interface (CNI) plug-in.
Create an Azure Standard Load Balancer.
Create an Azure Basic Load Balancer.

questions.explanation:
An AKS Ingress controller provides Layer 7 reverse-proxy routing and TLS termination for Kubernetes services. Together with Ingress rules, it can expose multiple services through a single IP address. Azure Load Balancer is a Layer 4 service and does not provide HTTP routing or TLS termination. [Microsoft Learn: AKS network best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/operator-best-practices-network)

**Learn more:** [Best practices for network resources in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/operator-best-practices-network)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant called contoso.com.  
  
You plan to create several security alerts by using Azure Monitor.  
  
You need to prepare the Azure subscription for these alerts.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
A Log Analytics workspace collects Azure AD audit and sign-in logs for analysis and supports log queries and alert rules for security events. Azure Storage and Event Hubs can receive exported logs, but they do not provide the Azure Monitor log-query alerting capability; an Automation account is not required to create these alerts.

**Learn more:** [Log Analytics workspace overview - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-workspace-overview) · [Monitor and report on security events in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/monitor-report-aad-security-events/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster that will connect to an Azure Container Registry.  
  
You need to authenticate to the Azure Container Registry by using the automatically generated service principal.  
  
What should you create?

options.text: an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) group
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) role assignment
an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) user
a secret in Azure Key Vault

questions.explanation:
Azure Container Registry access for a service principal is granted through an Azure RBAC role assignment scoped to the registry. The assignment gives the service principal pull permission, typically through the AcrPull role.

**Learn more:** [Azure Container Registry authentication with service principals](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-auth-service-principal) · [Azure Container Registry Microsoft Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has recently created an Azure subscription. You have subsequently been tasked with ensuring that you can secure Azure AD roles by using Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM).  
  
Which of the following actions should you take **FIRST**?

options.text: You should sign up Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for Azure AD roles.
You should consent to Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM).

questions.explanation:
PIM must first be consented to for the directory, which authorizes and enables the PIM service at the tenant level. Only afterward can the administrator complete identity verification and sign up PIM to manage Azure AD roles; role and resource discovery are subsequent activities.

**Learn more:** [Start using Privileged Identity Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-getting-started)

questions.explanation:
Azure Monitor metric alerts can use supported Log Analytics performance-counter data after it is converted to metrics. They support dimensional monitoring, near-real-time evaluation with frequencies as low as one minute, and stateful alerting, which sends a notification when the alert fires and again when it resolves. [Create metric alerts in Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-metric-logs)

**Learn more:** [Create metric alerts in Azure Monitor Logs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-metric-logs) · [Create Azure Monitor metric alert rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/alerts/alerts-create-metric-alert-rule)

You have an Azure subscription that contains an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster named AKS1.  
  
You have an Azure container registry that stores container images deployed by using Azure DevOps Microsoft-hosted agents.  
  
You need to ensure that administrators can access AKS1 only from specified networks. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure for AKS1?
questions.explanation:
AKS API server authorized IP address ranges allow only specified public IP addresses or CIDR ranges to reach the Kubernetes API server, blocking all other source addresses. This directly restricts administrative access to the designated networks with a control-plane access setting.

**Learn more:** [Secure access to the API server using authorized IP address ranges in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/api-server-authorized-ip-ranges)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription connected to an Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 1 tenant.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection.  
  
You need to ensure that you can configure both a user risk policy and a sign-in risk policy.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: Purchase Azure Active Directory Premium Plan 2 licenses for all users.
Register all users for Azure Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
Enable security defaults for Azure Active Directory.
Enable enhanced security features in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

questions.explanation:
User risk and sign-in risk policies are Azure AD Identity Protection capabilities that require Azure AD Premium P2 licensing; Premium P1 does not provide those risk-policy features. MFA registration may be needed later for self-remediation, but it does not enable the policies themselves.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra licensing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/licensing) · [Configure and enable risk policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management (Defender EASM) resource named EASM1.  
  
You review the Attack Surface Summary dashboard.  
  
You need to identify these insights:  
  
- Deprecated technologies that are no longer supported  
- Infrastructure that will expire soon  
  
Which dashboard section should you review?
questions.explanation:
The Attack surface priorities section lists security insights by severity. Its low-severity insights include deprecated technology that is no longer supported and infrastructure that is soon expiring.\
\
**Learn more:** [Understanding dashboards | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/external-attack-surface-management/understanding-dashboards)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You create a new virtual network called VNet1.  
  
You plan to deploy an Azure web app named App1 that will use VNet1 and be accessible through private IP addresses. The solution must support both inbound and outbound network traffic.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an Azure App Service Hybrid Connection.

questions.explanation:
An App Service Environment is a dedicated Azure App Service deployment within a virtual network. When configured with an internal virtual IP, its apps are reached through an address in the App Service Environment subnet, and its inbound and outbound application traffic remains within the selected virtual network. Regional virtual network integration supports outbound traffic only, not private inbound access.

**Learn more:** [App Service Environment networking](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/environment/networking) · [Create an App Service Environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/environment/creation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have been tasked with configuring an access review that you intend to assign to a new collection of reviews. You must also ensure that the reviews can be performed by resource owners.  
  
You begin by creating an access review program and an access review control.  
  
You now need to configure **Reviewers**. Which setting should you choose for **Reviewers**?
questions.explanation:
Resource owners are configured as reviewers by selecting **Group Owners**. Microsoft Entra access reviews supports group owners as reviewers for group reviews; these owners are the resource owners responsible for determining whether members should retain access.

**Learn more:** [Create an access review of groups and applications - Microsoft Entra ID Governance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/create-access-review) · [Plan a Microsoft Entra access reviews deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/deploy-access-reviews)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an Azure subscription named Subscription1 that contains a resource group named RG1 and the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783954295771-skqb01fn.png)  
  
You perform these tasks:  
  
- Assign User1 the Network Contributor role for Subscription1.  
- Assign User2 the Contributor role for RG1.  
  
Assign the following policy definition to Subscription1 and RG1: **External accounts with write permissions should be removed from your subscription.**  
  
What is the Compliance State of the policy assignments?

options.text: The Compliance State of both policy assignments is Non-compliant.
The Compliance State of the policy assignment to Subscription1 is Compliant, and the Compliance State of the policy assignment to RG1 is Non-compliant.
The Compliance State of the policy assignment to Subscription1 is Non-compliant, and the Compliance State of the policy assignment to RG1 is Compliant.
The Compliance State of both policy assignments is Compliant.

questions.explanation:
The built-in policy evaluates only resources of type `Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions` and uses an `AuditIfNotExists` check for the related Microsoft Defender for Cloud assessment. The guest accounts have write-capable role assignments, so the subscription-level assessment is unhealthy and the Subscription1 assignment is non-compliant. RG1 contains no subscription resource for this policy rule to evaluate, so the assignment at RG1 is compliant.

**Learn more:** [Azure built-in policy definition: Guest accounts with write permissions on Azure resources should be removed](https://github.com/Azure/azure-policy/blob/master/built-in-policies/policyDefinitions/Security%20Center/ASC_RemoveGuestAccountsWithWritePermissions_Audit.json) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud built-in policy definitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/policy-reference)

questions.question:
You have an Azure Container Registry named ContReg1 that contains a container image named image1.  
  
You enable content trust for ContReg1. After enabling content trust, you push two images to ContReg1 as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783954343798-plofb08a.png)  
  
Which images are trusted?
questions.explanation:
Azure Container Registry Docker Content Trust identifies trusted images by signed tags. Enabling content trust on a registry does not retroactively sign existing images. A push performed with client content trust enabled signs the image tag, whereas a push with client content trust disabled leaves it unsigned.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage signed images with Docker Content Trust in Azure Container Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-content-trust)

questions.question:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You also have an Amazon Web Services (AWS) account.  
  
You need to add the AWS account to Defender for Cloud.  
  
What should you do first?

options.text: From Defender for Cloud, configure the Environment settings.
From the AWS account, enable a security hub.
From Defender for Cloud, configure the Security solutions settings.
From the Azure portal, add the AWS enterprise application.

questions.explanation:
To connect an AWS account, begin in Microsoft Defender for Cloud by opening **Environment settings**. From there, select **Add environment** and then **Amazon Web Services** to start the connector onboarding workflow.\
\
**Learn more:** [Connect AWS accounts to Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/quickstart-onboard-aws)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a new stored access policy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A stored access policy controls only service SAS tokens that explicitly reference that policy. Creating a new policy does not invalidate existing SAS tokens or existing stored access policies. An ad hoc SAS that is not associated with a stored access policy can be immediately revoked only by regenerating the storage account key used to sign it.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a service SAS - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-service-sas) · [Define a stored access policy - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/define-stored-access-policy)

questions.question:
Solution: You create a lock on sa1.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Azure Resource Manager locks apply only to management-plane operations; they do not restrict storage data-plane operations. Existing SAS-based access to blobs and files therefore remains valid, so a lock does not revoke all access to the storage account.\
\
**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources) · [Apply an Azure Resource Manager lock to a storage account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/lock-account-resource)

questions.question:
Solution: You create new SASs.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
Creating new shared access signatures does not revoke existing SASs. Ad hoc SASs remain valid until they expire or the signing storage account key is regenerated; SASs tied to stored access policies are revoked by modifying or deleting the applicable policy.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create a service SAS - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-service-sas)

questions.question:
Solution: Regenerate the Azure Storage account access keys.  
  
Does this accomplish the goal?
questions.explanation:
Regenerating both Azure Storage account access keys invalidates SAS tokens created with those keys, including service SAS tokens associated with stored access policies, and prevents requests signed with the old keys from authorizing. This revokes the stated Blob and File service access paths.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage account access keys - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-keys-manage) · [Create a service SAS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/create-service-sas)

options.text: From Inbound access settings in Cross-tenant access settings, configure the B2B direct connect settings.
From External collaboration settings, configure the Collaboration restrictions settings.
From External collaboration settings, configure the Guest invite settings.
From Outbound access settings in Cross-tenant access settings, configure the B2B collaboration settings.

questions.explanation:
Outbound cross-tenant access settings control whether users in the local tenant can access applications in an external Microsoft Entra organization. Under **B2B collaboration**, the **External applications** tab supports allowing selected external applications, which creates the required allow list for contoso.com users accessing fabrikam.com apps.

**Learn more:** [Manage cross-tenant access settings for B2B collaboration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/cross-tenant-access-settings-b2b-collaboration)

questions.question:
You have an Azure web app called WebApp1.  
  
You upload a certificate to WebApp1. You need to make that certificate available to WebApp1's app code.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Add a user-assigned managed identity to WebApp1.
Add an app setting to the WebApp1 configuration.
Enable system-assigned managed identity for WebApp1.
Configure the TLS/SSL binding for WebApp1.

questions.explanation:
Azure App Service makes uploaded certificates available to application code when the `WEBSITE_LOAD_CERTIFICATES` app setting contains the certificate thumbprint, or `*` for all uploaded certificates. A TLS/SSL binding does not expose the certificate to the application runtime.\
\
**Learn more:** [Use TLS/SSL certificates in your application code - Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate-in-code)

You have several development teams that will build applications in Azure.  
  
You plan to create a standard development environment to deploy for each team.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that enforces resource locks across the development environments and ensures the locks are applied consistently.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
questions.explanation:
Azure Blueprints support assignment-level locking modes, including read-only and do-not-delete, for resources deployed by a blueprint assignment. A reusable blueprint can therefore deploy the standardized environment for each team and apply those locks consistently.

**Learn more:** [Understand resource locking in Azure Blueprints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/concepts/resource-locking) · [Overview of Azure Blueprints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/overview)

questions.question:
You must ensure that users are able to access VM0. The solution must satisfy the platform-protection requirements.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: On Firewall, configure a network traffic filtering rule.
On Firewall, configure a DNAT rule.

questions.explanation:
An Azure Firewall DNAT rule translates and filters inbound traffic directed to the firewall’s public IP address, forwarding the permitted traffic to a private IP address and port on the target virtual machine. This provides controlled inbound access to VM0 through the firewall.\
\
**Learn more:** [Filter inbound Internet traffic with Azure Firewall DNAT using the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/tutorial-firewall-dnat)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has an Active Directory forest containing a single domain named weylandindustries.com. It also has an Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant with the same name.  
  
After all on-premises identities have been synchronized to Azure AD, you learn that users whose `givenName` attribute begins with LAB must not be synchronized to Azure AD.  
  
Which action should you take?

options.text: You should make use of the Synchronization Rules Editor to create an attribute-based filtering rule.
You should configure a DNAT rule on the Firewall.
You should configure a network traffic filtering rule on the Firewall.
You should make use of Active Directory Users and Computers to create an attribute-based filtering rule.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync supports attribute-based filtering of directory objects by using synchronization rules in the Synchronization Rules Editor. A rule scoped to exclude users whose `givenName` starts with `LAB` prevents those objects from synchronizing to Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Configure filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-configure-filtering)

questions.question:
In the Azure portal, you are configuring an Azure Policy assignment.  
  
You plan to assign policies that use the DeployIfNotExist, AuditIfNotExist, Append, and Deny effects.  
  
Which effect requires a managed identity for the assignment?
questions.explanation:
The DeployIfNotExist effect deploys a template when the required related resource or configuration does not exist. Azure Policy uses the policy assignment’s managed identity, which must have appropriate RBAC permissions, to perform that deployment and remediation.\
\
**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deployIfNotExists effect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deploy-if-not-exists) · [Remediate non-compliant resources with Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/how-to/remediate-resources)
